notes.1: (sn): This statement may fit better with the final paragraph of 1 Kgs 22.

notes.2: (map): For location see Map2-B1; Map4-D3; Map5-E2; Map6-A4; Map7-C1.
notes.3: (tn, Heb): “and he sent messengers and said to them.”
notes.5: (sn): Apparently Baal Zebub refers to a local manifestation of the god Baal at the Philistine city of Ekron. The name appears to mean “Lord of the Flies,” but it may be a deliberate scribal corruption of Baal Zebul, “Baal, the Prince,” a title known from the Ugaritic texts. For further discussion and bibliography, see HALOT 261 s.v. זְבוּב בַּעַל and M. Cogan and H. Tadmor, II Kings (AB), 25.

rashi.heb:
*בְּעַד הַשְּׂבָכָה.* 
גראד"ה בְּלַעַ"ז. אוֹמֵר אֲנִי שֶׁרְגִילִים לְאָרְגוֹ שְׁתִי וָעֵרֶב בִּנְסָרִים אֲרֻכִּים וּקְצָרִים שֶׁקּוֹרִין קנטינל"י בְּלַעַ"ז, וְעוֹשִׂין נְקָבִים נְקָבִים כְּעֵין שְׂבָכָה, וְקָרוּי פרדונ"י בְּלַעַ"ז. וַאֲנִי שָׁמַעְתִּי 'שְׂבָכָה' ווי"ץ בְּלַעַ"ז, וּבִלְשׁוֹן אַשְׁכְּנַז שווינדל שטיג כְּמוֹ שֶׁפֵּרַשְׁתִּי וּבְלוּלִּים יַעֲלוּ.
rashi.eng: *through the lattice.* Heb. השבכה, grata in Medieval Latin, lattice. I say that they were accustomed to weave it as a warp and a woof with long boards and short ones, which is called lattes, lathe [in] Fr., cancelli [in Latin]; cancel in O.F., space behind the grating, and they would make it all of holes like a sort of net, and it is called prodne in O.F. And I heard that שְּׂבָכָה is vis in Fr. a screw, and in German schwindel stieg, a spiral staircase, as I explained in (I Kings 6:8): “and with winding stairs they would go up…”

rashi.heb:
*וַיָּחַל.* 
לְשׁוֹן חֹלִי.
rashi.eng: *and he became ill.* Heb. וַיָחַל an expression of sickness.

notes.6: (tn, Heb): “Is it because there is no God in Israel [that] you are going to inquire of Baal Zebub, the god of Ekron?” The translation seeks to bring out the sarcastic tone of the rhetorical question.

notes.7: (tn, Heb): “to him.” The narrative is elliptical and telescoped here. The account of Elijah encountering the messengers and delivering the Lord’s message is omitted; we only here of it as the messengers report what happened to the king.

notes.9: (tn, Heb): “Is it because there is no God in Israel [that] you are sending to inquire of Baal Zebub, the god of Ekron?” The translation seeks to bring out the sarcastic tone of the rhetorical question. In v. 3 the messengers are addressed (in the phrase “you are on your way” the second person plural pronoun is used in Hebrew), but here the king is addressed (in the phrase “you are sending” the second person singular pronoun is used).

notes.10: (tn, Heb): “he”; the referent (the king) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

notes.13: (tn, Heb): “an owner of hair.” This idiomatic expression indicates that Elijah was very hairy. For other examples where the idiom “owner of” is used to describe a characteristic of someone, see HALOT 143 s.v. בַּעַל. For example, an “owner of dreams” is one who frequently has dreams (Gen 37:19) and an “owner of anger” is a hot-tempered individual (Prov 22:24).
notes.14: (tn, Heb): “belt of skin” (i.e., one made from animal hide).
notes.15: (tn, Heb): “he”; the referent (the king) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

notes.16: (tn, Heb): “he”; the referent (the king) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
notes.17: (tn, Heb): “officer of fifty and his fifty.”
notes.19: (tn, Heb): “he”; the referent (the captain) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
notes.20: (sn): The prophet Elijah’s position on the top of the hill symbolizes his superiority to the king and his messengers.

notes.22: (tn, Heb): “answered and said to the officer of fifty.”
notes.23: (tn): Wordplay contributes to the irony here. The king tells Elijah to “come down” (Hebrew יָרַד, yarad), but Elijah calls fire down (יָרַד) on the arrogant king’s officer.

notes.24: (tn, Heb): “he”; the referent (the king) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
notes.25: (tc): The MT reads, “he answered and said to him.” The verb “he answered” (וַיַּעַן, vayya’an) is probably a corruption of “he went up” (וַיַּעַל, vayya’al). See v. 9.
notes.26: (sn): In this second panel of the three-paneled narrative, the king and his captain are more arrogant than before. The captain uses a more official sounding introduction (“this is what the king says”) and the king adds “at once” to the command.

notes.27: (tc): Two medieval Hebrew mss, the LXX, and the Syriac Peshitta have the singular “to him.”
notes.28: (tn): Or “intense fire.” The divine name may be used idiomatically to emphasize the intensity of the fire. Whether one translates אֱלֹהִים (’elohim) here as a proper name or idiomatically, this addition to the narrative (the name is omitted in the first panel, v. 10b) emphasizes the severity of the judgment and is appropriate given the more intense command delivered by the king to the prophet in this panel.

notes.29: (tn, Heb): “he”; the referent (the king) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
notes.30: (tn, Heb): “went up and approached and kneeled.”

notes.33: (sn): In this third panel the verb “come down” (יָרַד, yarad) occurs again, this time describing Elijah’s descent from the hill at the Lord’s command. The moral of the story seems clear: Those who act as if they have authority over God and his servants just may pay for their arrogance with their lives; those who, like the third commander, humble themselves and show the proper respect for God’s authority and for his servants will be spared and find God quite cooperative.

notes.34: (tn, Heb): “he”; the referent (Elijah) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
notes.35: (tn, Heb): “him”; the referent (the king) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
notes.36: (tn, Heb): “Because you sent messengers to inquire of Baal Zebub, the god of Ekron, is there no God in Israel to inquire of his word?”
notes.37: (sn): For the third time in this chapter we read the Lord’s sarcastic question to king and the accompanying announcement of judgment. The repetition emphasizes one of the chapter’s main themes. Israel’s leaders should seek guidance from their own God, not a pagan deity, for Israel’s sovereign God is the one who controls life and death.

notes.38: (tn, Heb): “according to the word of the Lord which he spoke through Elijah.”
notes.39: (tn, Heb): “Jehoram replaced him as king…because he had no son.” Some ancient textual witnesses add “his brother,” which was likely added on the basis of the statement later in the verse that Ahaziah had no son.

rashi.heb:
*וַיִּמְלֹךְ יְהוֹרָם תַּחְתָּיו.* 
אָחִיו הָיָה.
rashi.eng: *and Jehoram reigned in his stead.* He was his brother.

rashi.heb:
*בִּשְׁנַת שְׁתַּיִם לִיהוֹרָם בֶּן יְהוֹשָׁפָט.* 
אֶפְשָׁר לוֹמַר כֵּן, וַהֲלֹא מָלַךְ בִּשְׁנַת תְּשַׁע עֶשְׂרֵה לִיהוֹשָׁפָט, שֶׁהֲרֵי אֲחַזְיָה מָלַךְ בִּשְׁבַע עֶשְׂרֵה, וּמָלַךְ שְׁנָתַיִם, וּבְסָמוּךְ נָמֵי כְּתִיב: בִּשְׁנַת שְׁמוֹנֶה עֶשְׂרֵה לִיהוֹשָׁפָט מָלַךְ יְהוֹרָם, וִיהוֹשָׁפָט מָלַךְ עֶשְׂרִים וְחָמֵשׁ שָׁנִים קֹדֶם שֶׁמָּלַךְ יְהוֹרָם בְּנוֹ, אֶלָּא רָאוּי הָיָה יְהוֹשָׁפָט לֵהָרֵג בְּרָמוֹת גִּלְעָד, וּבִשְׂכַר שֶׁזָּעַק, תָּלָה לוֹ שֶׁבַע שָׁנִים, וּמֵאוֹתָהּ שָׁעָה הוּא מוֹנֶה לִבְנוֹ.
rashi.eng: *in the second year of Jehoram the son of Jehoshaphat.* Is it possible to say this? Did he not reign in the nineteenth year of Jehoshaphat, for Ahaziah reigned in the seventeenth [year of Jehoshaphat] (I Kings 22:52), and reigned for two years (ibid.), and in a nearby chapter also it is written (3:1) In the eighteenth year of Jehoshaphat, Jehoram reigned. Now Jehoshaphat reigned twenty-five years before Jehoram his son reigned. But, Jehoshaphat was deservant of being killed in Ramoth Gilead, but as a reward for his crying out [to God,] God suspended his death for him seven years, and from that time Scripture counts [the years] to his son.

notes.40: (tn, Heb): “As for the rest of the acts of Ahaziah which he did, are they not recorded in the scroll of the events of the days of the kings of Israel?”

rashi.heb:
*בַּסְעָרָה.* 
בְּרוּחַ סְעָרָה.
rashi.eng: *in a whirlwind.* [lit. in a storm],] i.e., in a storm wind.

notes.42: (map): For location see Map4-G4; Map5-C1; Map6-E3; Map7-D1; Map8-G3.

rashi.heb:
*שֵׁב נָא פֹה.* 
חָפֵץ הָיָה לִדְחוֹתוֹ מֵחֲמַת עֲנָוָה, שֶׁלֹּא יִרְאֶה בְּהִלָּקְחוֹ.
rashi.eng: *Stay here now.* He wished to drive him away because of his [Elijah’s] humility, so that he would not see him being taken away.

notes.44: (tn, Heb): “from your head.” The same expression occurs in v. 5.

rashi.heb:
*אֶת אֲדֹנֶיךָ.* 
וְלֹא אֲדוֹנֵנוּ, מְלַמֵּד שֶׁהָיוּ שְׁקוּלִים כְּאֵלִיָּהוּ.
rashi.eng: *your master.* but not our master. This teaches us that they were equal to Elijah.

notes.45: (map): For location see Map5-B2; Map6-E1; Map7-E1; Map8-E3; Map10-A2; Map11-A1.

notes.46: (tn, Heb): “the two of them.” The referents (Elijah and Elisha) have been specified in the translation for clarity.

rashi.heb:
*וַיִּגְלֹם.* 
כְּרָכָהּ, כְּדֵי שֶׁתְּהֵא נוֹחָה לְהַכּוֹת בָּהּ.
rashi.eng: *and rolled it up.* He rolled it up in order that it would be easy to strike with it.

rashi.heb:
*וַיִּגְלֹם.* 
וְלֹא כְּרִיכָה מַמָּשׁ, אֶלָּא קוֹלֵט, שֶׁקּוֹרִין פייגד"ו בְּלַעַ"ז.
rashi.eng: *and he rolled it.* not exactly rolling but gathering together, which is called koulir in O.F.

notes.47: (tn, Heb): “Ask! What can I do for you….?”
notes.48: (tn, Heb): “May a double portion of your spirit come to me.”

notes.49: (tn, Heb): “he”; the referent (Elijah) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

rashi.heb:
*הִקְשִׁיתָ לִשְׁאוֹל.* 
אִי אֶפְשָׁר לָתֵת לְךָ יוֹתֵר מִמַּה שֶּׁיֵּשׁ לִי בְּיָדִי.
rashi.eng: *You have made a difficult request.* It is impossible to give you more than I have in my possession.

rashi.heb:
*אִם תִּרְאֶה אֹתִי לֻקַּח מֵאִתָּךְ.* 
אָז אוּכַל לַעֲשׂוֹת לְךָ יוֹתֵר וְיוֹתֵר.
rashi.eng: *If you see me taken away from you.* then I will be able to do for you more and more.

rashi.heb:
*יְהִי לְךָ כֵן וְאִם אַיִן לֹא יִהְיֶה.* 
שֶׁאֵין הַיְכֹלֶת בְּיָדִי.
rashi.eng: *it will be so to you, and if not, it will not be.* for I have not the ability.

notes.51: (tn): Though the noun is singular here, it may be collective, in which case it could be translated “chariots.”
notes.52: (tn, Heb): “look, a chariot of fire and horses of fire.”
notes.53: (tn, Heb): “and they made a division between the two of them.”

notes.54: (sn): Elisha may be referring to the fiery chariot(s) and horses as the Lord’s spiritual army that fights on behalf of Israel (see 2 Kgs 6:15-17; 7:6). However, the juxtaposition with “my father” (clearly a reference to Elijah as Elisha’s mentor), and the parallel in 2 Kgs 13:14 (where the king addresses Elisha with these words), suggest that Elisha is referring to Elijah. In this case Elijah is viewed as a one man army, as it were. When the Lord spoke through him, his prophetic word was as powerful as an army of chariots and horses. See M. A. Beek, “The Meaning of the Expression ‘The Chariots and Horsemen of Israel’ (II Kings ii 12),” The Witness of Tradition (OTS 17), 1-10.

rashi.heb:
*אָבִי אָבִי רֶכֶב יִשְׂרָאֵל.* 
רַבִּי רַבִּי דְּטָב לְהוֹן לְיִשְׂרָאֵל בִּצְלוֹתֵהּ מֵרְתִיכִין וּפָרָשִׁין.
rashi.eng: *My father! My father! The chariots of Israel.* Jonathan [renders:] My master! My master! Who benefited Israel with his prayer more than chariots and riders.

notes.55: (tn, Heb): “Elijah’s cloak, which had fallen off him.” The wording is changed slightly in the translation for the sake of variety of expression (see v. 13).

rashi.heb:
*אַיֵּה ה' אֱלֹהֵי אֵלִיָּהוּ.* 
שֶׁהֻבְטַחְתִּי שֶׁתִּשְׁרֶה בִי פִּי שְׁנַיִם בְּרוּחוֹ אֵלַי.
rashi.eng: *Where is the Lord, the God of Elijah?.* that I was promised [who promised me: Kara] that a double portion of his spirit would rest upon me.

rashi.heb:
*אַף הוּא וַיַּכֶּה אֶת הַמַּיִם.* 
אַף הוּא, בְּפִרְקֵי רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר, בְּנוֹ שֶל רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי: גְּדוֹלָה חֲצִיַּת אֱלִישָׁע כִּפְלַיִם כְּשֶׁל אֵלִיָּהוּ, שֶׁבִּתְחִלָּה זְכוּת שְׁנֵיהֶם, וְעַכְשָׁיו זְכוּתוֹ יְחִידִי.
rashi.eng: *He too struck the water.* He too. In the Chapters of Rabbi Eliezer the son of Rabbi Jose the Galilean, [should read: In the Thirty-two Methods of Rabbi Eliezer the son of Rabbi Jose the Galilean. Shem Ephraim], Elisha’s splitting [the Jordan] was doubly as great as Elijah’s, for in the beginning there was the merit of them both, while here was his merit alone.

notes.56: (map): For location see Map5-B2; Map6-E1; Map7-E1; Map8-E3; Map10-A2; Map11-A1.
notes.57: (tn, Heb): “and the sons of the prophets who were in Jericho, [who were standing] opposite, saw him and said.”

notes.60: (tn, Heb): “he”; the referent (Elisha) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

rashi.heb:
*פֶּן נְשָׂאוֹ רוּחַ ה'.* 
אֶפְשָׁר אֶמֶשׁ אָמְרוּ לוֹ: הֲיָדַעְתָּ כִּי הַיּוֹם ה' לוֹקֵחַ אֶת אֲדוֹנֶיךָ, וְעַכְשָׁיו נֶעְלָם מֵהֶם הֵיכָן הוּא, מְלַמֵּד, מִיּוֹם שֶׁנִּגְנַז אֵלִיָּהוּ הָלְכָה וְנִסְתַּלְּקָה רוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ מִן הַנְּבִיאִים, וְשׁוּב לֹא הָיְתָה רוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ מְרֻבָּה בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל.
rashi.eng: *Perhaps a wind from the Lord has carried him off.* Is it possible that on the day before, they said to him, “Do you know that today the Lord will take your master from you?” (v. 5) And now they did not know where he was? This teaches us that since the day when Elijah was hidden, the holy spirit departed from the prophets, and the holy spirit was no longer widespread throughout Israel.

notes.61: (tn, Heb): “him”; the referent (Elijah) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

rashi.heb:
*עַד בּשׁ.* 
נִתְבַּיֵּשׁ מֵהֶם, שֶׁלֹּא יֹאמְרוּ אֵינוֹ רוֹצֶה לְהַקְבִּיל פְּנֵי רַבּוֹ, לְפִי שֶׁנָּטַל גְּדֻלָּתוֹ אֵינוֹ רוֹצֶה שֶׁיָּשׁוּב, כָּל זֶה רָאִיתִי בַּתּוֹסֶפְתָּא דְּסוֹטָה.
rashi.eng: *until he was ashamed.* He was ashamed because of them, lest they say that he does not want to go to meet his teacher. Since he took over his high position, he does not want him to return. All this I saw in Tosefta Sotah (12:5).

notes.62: (tn, Heb): “he”; the referent (Elisha) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

rashi.heb:
*וְהַמַּיִם רָעִים.* 
וּמֵחֲמַת הַמַּיִם הָאָרֶץ מְשַׁכֶּלֶת אֶת יוֹשְׁבֶיהָ לְקָבְרָם, אִם כֵּן מַהוּ: וּמוֹשַׁב הָעִיר טוֹב, מִכָּאן אָמְרוּ: חֵן מָקוֹם עַל יוֹשְׁבָיו.
rashi.eng: *but the water is bad.* and because of the water, the land causes people to die, to send them to their graves. If so, what is the meaning of: “the city is a good place to live in?” From here we deduce that a place has charm for its inhabitants.

notes.65: (tn, Heb): “he”; the referent (Elisha) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

notes.67: (tn, Heb): “there will no longer be from there death and miscarriage [or, ‘barrenness’].”

rashi.heb:
*אֶל מוֹצָא הַמַּיִם.* 
שֶׁהָיוּ נוֹבְעִים מִשָּׁם.
rashi.eng: *to the source of the water.* from where the water flowed.

rashi.heb:
*וַיַּשְׁלֶךְ שָׁם מֶלַח.* 
וַהֲלֹא מֶלַח דָּבָר הַמְקַלְקֵל אֶת הַמַּיִם הוּא, אֶלָּא נֵס בְּתוֹךְ נֵס.
rashi.eng: *and threw salt there.*

notes.68: (tn, Heb): “according to the word of Elisha which he spoke.”

notes.69: (map): For location see Map4-G4; Map5-C1; Map6-E3; Map7-D1; Map8-G3.
notes.70: (tn): The word נַעַר (na’ar), here translated “boy,” can refer to a broad age range, including infants as well as young men. But the qualifying term “young” (or “small”) suggests these youths were relatively young. The phrase in question (“young boy”) occurs elsewhere in 1 Sam 20:35; 1 Kgs 3:7 (used by Solomon in an hyperbolic manner); 11:17; 2 Kgs 5:14; and Isa 11:6.

rashi.heb:
*וּנְעָרִים קְטַנִּים.* 
הַמְנֹעָרִין מִן הַמִּצְוֹת.
rashi.eng: *and some little boys.* Heb. וּנְעָרִים, people empty [of any observance of commandments].

rashi.heb:
*עֲלֵה קֵרֵחַ.* 
עֲלֵה מִכָּאן, שֶׁהִקְרַחְתָּ עָלֵינוּ אֶת הַמָּקוֹם, שֶׁעַד עַכְשָׁיו הָיִינוּ מִשְׂתַּכְּרִין לְהָבִיא מַיִם מְתוּקִים מֵרָחוֹק, וּמִתְפַּרְנְסִין בְּכָךְ, וּמִשֶּׁהִמְתִּיקוּ אִבְּדוּ פַּרְנָסָתָן, כָּךְ מְפֹרָשׁ בְּסוֹטָה.
rashi.eng: *Go away, baldy.* Go away from here, for you have made the place bald for us, for until now we would hire ourselves out to bring sweet water from a distance, and we would earn our livelihood thereby. And when the water became sweet, they lost their livelihood. Thus it is explained in Sotah (46b).

notes.71: (tn, Heb): “he cursed them in the name of the Lord.” A curse was a formal appeal to a higher authority (here the Lord) to vindicate one’s cause through judgment. As in chapter one, this account makes it clear that disrespect for the Lord’s designated spokesmen can be deadly, for it is ultimately rejection of the Lord’s authority.

rashi.heb:
*וַיִּרְאֵם.* 
רָאָה שֶׁאֵין בָּהֶם וְלֹא בְּזַרְעָם לַחְלוּחִית שֶל טוֹבָה.
rashi.eng: *and saw them.* He saw that neither in them nor in their descendants would there be any ‘sap’ of good deeds.

notes.72: (sn): The two brief episodes recorded in vv. 19-25 demonstrate Elisha’s authority and prove that he is the legitimate prophetic heir of Elijah. He has the capacity to bring life and blessing to those who recognize his authority, or death and judgment to those who reject him. For location see Map2-B1; Map4-D3; Map5-E2; Map6-A4; Map7-C1.

notes.73: (map): For location see Map2-B1; Map4-D3; Map5-E2; Map6-A4; Map7-C1.

rashi.heb:
*וִיהוֹרָם בֶּן אַחְאָב.* 
אַף פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ, בִּשְׁבִיל לְהַגִּיד נֵס שֶל מֵישָׁע מֶלֶךְ מוֹאָב שֶׁנַּעֲשָׂה עַל יְדֵי אֱלִישָׁע נִכְתְּבָה כָּאן, שֶׁמָּנָה בְּאֵלִיָּהוּ שְׁמוֹנָה נִסִּים, וּבֶאֱלִישָׁע שִׁשָּׁה עָשָׂר, לְקַיֵּם: פִּי שְׁנַיִם בְּרוּחֲךָ אֵלַי, וּכְתָבָן כֻּלָּם זוֹ בְּצַד זוֹ, כָּךְ רָאִיתִי בִּשְׁלשִׁים וּשְׁתַּיִם מִדּוֹת דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בְּנוֹ דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי, וַחֲצִיַּת יַרְדֵּן שֶׁל אֱלִישָׁע, כִּשְׁתַּיִם דְּשֶׁל אֵלִיָּהוּ.
rashi.eng: *And Jehoram the son of Ahab.* This section too was written here to tell the miracle of Mesha the king of Moab, which was performed through Elisha, for Scripture enumerated for Elijah eight miracles and for Elisha sixteen, to fulfill “a double portion of your spirit to me” (above 2:9), and he wrote them all one juxtaposed to the other. I saw this in the Thirty-two Methods of R. Eliezer the son of R. Jose the Calilean. Now the dividing of the Jordan by Elisha is counted like two miracles of Elijah.

rashi.heb:
*רַק לֹא כְאָבִיו וּכְאִמּוֹ.* 
שֶׁהוֹסִיפוּ אֶת הַבַּעַל, לְהַכְעִיס.
rashi.eng: *however, not like his father and mother.* who added the worship of the Baal in order to provoke God.

notes.76: (tc): The Hebrew text has the singular, “it.” Some ancient witnesses read the plural, which seems preferable since the antecedent (“sins”) is plural. Another option is to emend the plural “sins” to a singular. One ancient Greek witness has the singular “sin.”

rashi.heb:
*רַק בְּחַטֹּאות יָרָבְעָם וְגוֹ'.* 
דָּבֵק. וְכֵן כָּל מַלְכֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל, מִדְּאָגָה שֶׁלֹּא תָשׁוּב הַמַּמְלָכָה לְבֵית דָּוִד אִם יַעֲלוּ לָרֶגֶל, לְכָךְ עָבְדוּ אֶת הָעֲגָלִים.
rashi.eng: *Only to the sins of Jeroboam… did he cling.* And so [did] all kings of Israel, for fear lest the kingdom return to the house of David if they would perform the pilgrimage on festivals. They, therefore, worshipped the calves.

notes.77: (tn): For a discussion of the meaning of term (נֹקֵד, noqed), see M. Cogan and H. Tadmor, II Kings (AB), 43.
notes.78: (tn): The vav + perfect here indicates customary action contemporary with the situation described in the preceding main clause. See IBHS 533-34 �32.2.3e.

rashi.heb:
*נֹקֵד.* 
מָרֵי גֵיתִין.
rashi.eng: *a sheepman.* Jonathan [however, renders נֹקֵד as] an owner of livestock.

rashi.heb:
*אֵילִים צָמֶר.* 
דִּיכְרִין דְּרָעֲיָא, עִם צִמְרָם.
rashi.eng: *rams with their wool.* Jonathan [renders:] pasture-fed rams, i.e., with their wool.

notes.80: (tn, Heb): “he”; the referent (Jehoshaphat) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
notes.81: (tn, Heb): “I will go up – like me, like you; like my people, like your people; like my horses; like your horses.”

notes.82: (tn, Heb): “Where is the road we will go up?”
notes.83: (tn, Heb): “he”; the referent (Jehoram) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

rashi.heb:
*דֶּרֶךְ מִדְבַּר אֱדוֹם.* 
כִּי גַּם מֶלֶךְ אֱדוֹם יֵלֵךְ עִמָּנוּ.
rashi.eng: *by way of the Desert of Edom.* for the king of Edom, too, will go with us.

notes.84: (tn, Heb): “the king of Israel and the king of Judah and the king of Edom.”

rashi.heb:
*לָתֵת אוֹתָם וְגוֹ'.* 
שֶׁיָּמוּתוּ בַּצָּמָא.
rashi.eng: *to deliver them….* for they will die of thirst.

notes.86: (tn, Heb): “that we might inquire of the Lord through him?”
notes.87: (tn, Heb): “who poured water on the hands of Elijah.” This refers to one of the typical tasks of a servant.

rashi.heb:
*אֲשֶׁר יָצַק מַיִם עַל יְדֵי אֵלִיָּהוּ.* 
בְּהַר הַכַּרְמֶל, וּבִיצִיקָתוֹ נַעֲשׂוּ אֶצְבְּעוֹתָיו כְּמַעְיְנוֹת מַיִם, עַד שֶׁנִּתְמַלְּאָה הַתְּעָלָה, וְרָאוּי הוּא לֵעָשׂוֹת לָנוּ נֵס עַל יָדוֹ בְּמַיִם.
rashi.eng: *who poured water on Elijah’s hands.* on Mt. Carmel, and with his pouring, his fingers became like springs of water, until the ditch filled up, and it is fitting for a miracle to be performed for us through him concerning water.

notes.88: (tn, Heb): “the word of the Lord is with him.”

notes.89: (tn): Or “What do we have in common?” The text reads literally, “What to me and to you?”

rashi.heb:
*אַל כִּי קָרָא ה' וְגוֹ'.* 
בְּבָעוּ לָא תִּדְכַּר חוֹבִין רִשְׁעָתָא הַהִיא, בָּעֵי עֲלָנָא רַחֲמִין, אֲרֵי זַמִּין ה' וְכוּ'.
rashi.eng: *Don’t [say that], for the Lord has summoned….* Jonathan [paraphrases thus]: Please do not mention the sins of that wicked woman. Beg mercy for us, for the Lord has summoned…

notes.92: (tn, Heb): “if I did not lift up the face of Jehoshaphat the king of Judah.”
notes.93: (tn, Heb): “I would not look at you or see you.”

notes.94: (tn): The term used refers to one who plays a stringed instrument, perhaps a harp.
notes.95: (tn, Heb): “the hand of the Lord came on him.” This may refer to what typically happened, “[for] when a musician played, the hand of the Lord would come upon him.”

rashi.heb:
*קְחוּ לִי מְנַגֵּן.* 
מִפְּנֵי הַכַּעַס נִסְתַּלְּקָה שְׁכִינָה מִמֶּנּוּ.
rashi.eng: *fetch me a musician.* Because of his anger, the Shechinah left him.

notes.96: (tn, Heb): “making this valley cisterns, cisterns.” The Hebrew noun גֵּב (gev) means “cistern” in Jer 14:3 (cf. Jer 39:10). The repetition of the noun is for emphasis. See GKC 396 �123.e. The verb (“making”) is an infinitive absolute, which has to be interpreted in light of the context. The translation above takes it in an imperatival sense. The command need not be understood as literal, but as hyperbolic. Telling them to build cisterns is a dramatic way of leading into the announcement that he would miraculously provide water in the desert. Some prefer to translate the infinitive as an imperfect with the Lord as the understood subject, “I will turn this valley [into] many pools.”

rashi.heb:
*גֵּבִים גֵּבִים.* 
בּוֹרוֹת מְלֵאִים מַיִם.
rashi.eng: *full of pools.* Pits full of water.

notes.98: (tn, Heb): “and this is easy in the eyes of the Lord.”

rashi.heb:
*וְנָקַל זֹאת.* 
וְעוֹד נֵס זֶה נָקֵל וּמוּעָט בְּעֵינֵי ה', וְהוֹסִיף לְהַפְלִיא אֶתְכֶם נֵס אַחֵר, וְנָתַן אֶת מוֹאָב בְּיֶדְכֶם.
rashi.eng: *And this will be slight.* And furthermore, this miracle is slight and insignificant in the eyes of the Lord, and He will proceed to act wondrously with you [and perform] another miracle, and He will deliver Moab into your hands.

notes.100: (tn): Elisha places the object first and uses an imperfect verb form. The stylistic shift may signal that he is now instructing them what to do, rather than merely predicting what would happen.
notes.102: (tn, Heb): “and ruin every good portion with stones.”

rashi.heb:
*וְכָל עֵץ טוֹב תַּפִּילוּ.* 
אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: לֹא תַשְׁחִית אֶת עֵצָהּ, כָּאן הִתִּיר לָכֶם, שֶׁהִיא אֻמָּה בְּזוּיָה וְנִקְלֵית לְפָנָיו, וְכֵן הוּא אוֹמֵר: לֹא תִדְרשׁ שְׁלוֹמָם וְטוֹבָתָם, אֵלּוּ הָאִילָנוֹת הַטּוֹבִים שֶׁבָּהֶם.
rashi.eng: *and you shall fell every good tree.* Even though it is stated (Deut. 20:19): “You shall not destroy its trees,” here He permitted it for you, for this is a contemptible and insignificant nation before Him. And so [Scripture] states (Deut. 23:7): “You shall not seek their welfare and their good.” These are the good trees that are among them.

rashi.heb:
*הַחֶלְקָה הַטּוֹבָה.* 
שָׂדֶה זְרוּעָה, קומצ"י בְּלַעַ"ז.
rashi.eng: *good field.* A sown field (Koumici in O.F.).

notes.103: (tn, Heb): “and in the morning, when the offering is offered up, look, water was coming from the way of Edom, and the land was filled with water.”

rashi.heb:
*וַיְהִי בַבֹּקֶר.* 
כַּעֲלוֹת הַמִּנְחָה. הַמַּיִם הִתְחִילוּ לֵירֵד מִן הַשָּׁמַיִם בַּבֹּקֶר בְּאֶרֶץ אֱדוֹם, וְכַעֲלוֹת הַמִּנְחָה בָּאִין שׁוֹטְפִין וּבָאִין לְאוֹתוֹ הַנַּחַל, לְפִי שֶׁאָמַר: לֹא תִרְאוּ רוּחַ וְלֹא תִרְאוּ גֶשֶׁם, בְּמִדְרַשׁ רַבִּי תַּנְחוּמָא.
rashi.eng: *And it was in the morning when the meal offering was offered up.* The water began falling from heaven in the morning in the land of Edom, and at the time of offering up the meal offering, it came surging into that valley, since the prophet had said, “You shall not see wind neither shall you see rain” (v. 17). In R. Tanhuma’s Midrash.

notes.104: (tn, Heb): “had come up to fight them.”
notes.105: (tn, Heb): “and they mustered all who tied on a belt and upwards, and they stood at the border.”

rashi.heb:
*עַל הַגְּבוּל.* 
עַל הַסְּפָר, שֶׁקּוֹרִין מרק"א.
rashi.eng: *at the border.* at the border that is called marche [in French].

rashi.heb:
*אֲדֻמִּים כַּדָּם.* 
כֵּן דֶּרֶךְ הַמַּיִם, כְּשֶׁהַשֶּׁמֶשׁ זוֹרַחַת עֲלֵיהֶם בַּבֹּקֶר, מַאֲדִימוֹת.
rashi.eng: *red as blood.* Such is the nature of water; when the sun shines on it in the morning, it appears red.

rashi.heb:
*מִנֶּגֶד.* 
מֵרָחוֹק, וְהֵם לֹא רָאוּ בְּאוֹתוֹ הַנַּחַל מַיִם מֵעוֹלָם, לְפִיכָךְ הָיוּ סְבוּרִין שֶׁהוּא דָם.
rashi.eng: *a distance.* at a distance. Now, since they had never seen water in that valley, they, therefore, thought that it was blood.

notes.106: (tn, Heb): “they”; the referent (the Moabites) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
notes.107: (tn): The translation assumes the verb is חָרַב (kharav, “to be desolate”). The infinitive absolute precedes the finite verb form for emphasis. (For another example of the Hophal infinitive with a Niphal finite verb, see Lev 19:20. Cf. also IBHS 582 �35.2.1c.) Some prefer to derive the verb from a proposed homonym meaning “at HALOT 349 s.v. II חרב and BDB 352 s.v. חָרְבָה).

notes.109: (tc): The consonantal text (Kethib) suggests, “and they went, striking down,” but the marginal reading (Qere) is “they struck down, striking down.” For a discussion of the textual problem, see M. Cogan and H. Tadmor, II Kings (AB), 46.

notes.110: (tn, Heb): “and [on] every good portion they were throwing each man his stone and they filled it.” The vav + perfect (“and they filled”) here indicates customary action contemporary with the situation described in the preceding main clause (where a customary imperfect is used, “they were throwing”). See the note at 3:4.
notes.111: (tn, Heb): “until he had allowed its stones to remain in Kir Hareseth.”

rashi.heb:
*וְהֶעָרִים יַהֲרֹסוּ.* 
הָיוּ הוֹרְסִין.
rashi.eng: *And they demolished the cities.* [i.e.,] they were demolishing the cities.

rashi.heb:
*יַשְׁלִיכוּ אִישׁ אַבְנוֹ.* 
שֶׁהָיוּ נוֹטְלִין הָאֲבָנִים מִן הַחוֹמוֹת, עַד הִשְׁאִיר כָּל אַבְנֵי הַקִּירוֹת בַּקִּיר לַעֲמֹד עַל חַרְסִית שֶׁלָּהֶן הוּא הַטִּיט, כְּלוֹמַר שֶׁלֹּא הָיְתָה עוֹד אֶבֶן בַּחוֹמָה, וְאַחֲרֵי זֹאת וַיָּסֹבּוּ הַקַּלָּעִים וַיַּכּוּ אֶת הַנִּשְׁאָר בַּחֶלְקָה, שֶׁלֹּא נִשְׁבְּרָה הַחוֹמָה, וְהִפִּילוּהָ.
rashi.eng: *and the catapultists surrounded and struck it.* and each one threw his stone for they would take stones from the walls until they left all the stones of the walls in the wall with only their clay, i.e., their mortar; that is to say that there were no more stones in the wall. And afterwards the catapultists surrounded that which remained in the field where the wall was not broken, and broke it down.

notes.112: (tn, Heb): “and the king of Moab saw that the battle was too strong for him.”
notes.113: (tn, Heb): “he took with him seven hundred men, who drew the sword, to break through against.”

notes.114: (tn, Heb): “there was great anger against Israel.” The meaning of this statement is uncertain, for the subject of the anger is not indicated. Except for two relatively late texts, the noun קֶצֶף (qetsef) refers to an outburst of divine anger. But it seems unlikely the Lord would be angry with Israel, for he placed his stamp of approval on the campaign (vv. 16-19). D. N. Freedman suggests the narrator, who obviously has a bias against the Omride dynasty, included this observation to show that the Lord would not allow the Israelite king to “have an undiluted victory” (as quoted in M. Cogan and H. Tadmor, II Kings [AB], 52, n. 8). Some suggest that the original source identified Chemosh the Moabite god as the subject and that his name was later suppressed by a conscientious scribe, but this proposal raises more questions than it answers. For a discussion of various views, see M. Cogan and H. Tadmor, II Kings (AB), 47-48, 51-52.

rashi.heb:
*וַיִּקַּח אֶת בְּנוֹ הַבְּכוֹר.* 
בִּפְסִיקְתָּא דְּפָרָשַׁת שְׁקָלִים נִדְרָשׁ: שֶׁשָּׁאַל אֶת עֲבָדָיו מַה טִּיבָהּ שֶל אֻמָּה זוֹ שֶׁנַּעֲשָׂה לָהֶם נִסִּים כָּאֵלֶּה, אָמְרוּ לוֹ: אֲבִיהֶם אַבְרָהָם בֵּן יָחִיד הָיָה לוֹ, אָמַר לוֹ הַקָּבָּ"ה הַקְרִיבֵהוּ לְפָנַי, וְרָצָה לְהַקְרִיבוֹ לְהַקָּבָּ"ה, אָמַר לָהֶם: אַף אֲנִי בֵּן בְּכוֹר יֵשׁ לִי, אֵלֵךְ וְאַקְרִיבֶנּוּ לַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה.
rashi.eng: *And he took his firstborn son.* In the Pesikta of the section of Shekalim it is expounded that he asked his servants ([in] Pesikta [and] Yalkut: his astrologers), “What is the character of this nation, that miracles such as these were performed for them?” They replied, “Their forefather, Abraham, had an only son. The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to him, Sacrifice him before Me, and he wanted to sacrifice him to the Holy One, Blessed be He.” He said to them, “I too have a first born son. I will go and sacrifice him to the gods.”

rashi.heb:
*עַל הַחֹמָה.* 
חָסֵר וָא"ו, שֶׁהָיָה עוֹבֵד לַחַמָּה.
rashi.eng: *on the wall.* Heb. חֹמָה. The ‘vav’ is missing, for he worshipped the sun, חַמָה [i.e., he sacrificed his son to the sun].

rashi.heb:
*וַיְהִי קֶצֶף גָּדוֹל.* 
שֶׁנִּזְכְּרוּ עֲוֹנוֹתֵיהֶם, שֶׁאַף הֵם עוֹבְדִין לַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה, וְאֵינָן רְאוּיִין לְנֵס.
rashi.eng: *and there was great wrath.* For their iniquities were remembered, that they too worship pagan deities and are not worthy of miracles.

notes.116: (tn, Heb): “a wife from among the wives of the sons of the prophets.”
notes.118: (tn, Heb): “your servant feared the Lord.” “Fear” refers here to obedience and allegiance, the products of healthy respect for the Lord’s authority.

rashi.heb:
*מִנְּשֵׁי בְנֵי הַנְּבִיאִים.* 
אֵשֶׁת עוֹבַדְיָה הָיְתָה. כָּל 'בְּנֵי הַנְּבִיאִים' שֶׁבַּמִּקְרָא, תַּרְגּוּמוֹ: תַּלְמִידֵי נְבִיַּיָּא.
rashi.eng: *of the wives of the disciples of the prophets.* She was the wife of Obadiah. Every expression of b’nei han’viim, the sons of the prophets, in Scripture, is translated in Targum as the disciples of the prophets.

rashi.heb:
*וְהַנּשֶׁה.* 
הוּא יְהוֹרָם בֶּן אַחְאָב, שֶׁהָיָה מַלְוֵהוּ בְּרִבִּית מַה שֶּׁזָּן אֶת הַנְּבִיאִים בִּימֵי אָבִיו, בְּמִדְרַשׁ רַבִּי תַּנְחוּמָא. לְכָךְ נֶאֱמַר: וַיַּךְ אֶת יְהוֹרָם בֵּין זְרוֹעָיו, שֶׁפָּשְׁטוּ לִטֹּל רִבִּית.
rashi.eng: *and the creditor.* He was Jehoram the son of Ahab, who would lend him with interest what he used to sustain the prophets in his father’s time. In R. Tanhuma’s Midrash (Mishpatim 9): Therefore it is stated (below 9:24): “And he struck Jehoram between his arms which stretched out to take interest.”

rashi.heb:
*אָסוּךְ שָׁמֶן.* 
כְּדֵי סִיכַת שֶׁמֶן, וְהָאָלֶ"ף בַּתֵּבָה מִן הַיְּסוֹד, כְּמוֹ אָלֶ"ף שֶל וְאַחְוָתִי בְּאָזְנֵיכֶם, וְהָאָלֶ"ף שֶׁל אִבְחַת חָרֶב.
rashi.eng: *a jug of oil.* enough oil for anointment, yet the “aleph” is part of the root like the aleph of (Job 13:17) and my speech in your ears, [Heb. וְאַחְוָתִי, from חוה], and the “aleph” of (Ezek. 21:20) the crying of [those struck down] by the sword, [Heb. אִבְחַת, from נבח], to bark.

notes.119: (tn, Heb): “Go, ask for containers from outside, from all your neighbors, empty containers.”
notes.120: (tn, Heb): “Do not borrow just a few.”

rashi.heb:
*וְסָגַרְתְּ הַדֶּלֶת.* 
כְּבוֹד הַנֵּס הוּא לָבֹא בְּהֶצְנֵעַ.
rashi.eng: *And you shall close the door.* It affords respect to the miracle if it comes about in secret.

rashi.heb:
*וְהַמָּלֵא תַּסִּיעִי.* 
מִלְּפָנַיִךְ, וְתִתְּנִי כְּלִי אַחֵר בִּמְקוֹמוֹ לְמַלּאוֹתוֹ, וּצְלוֹחִית הַשֶּׁמֶן לֹא תָזִיזִי מִמְּקוֹמוֹ, לְפִי שֶׁהַקָּבָּ"ה עוֹשֵׂהוּ כְּמַעְיָן, וְאֵין דֶּרֶךְ מַעְיָן לְזוּזוֹ מִמְּקוֹמוֹ, מִדְרַשׁ אַגָּדָה שָׁמַעְתִּי.
rashi.eng: *and the full one you shall carry away.* from before you, and you shall place another vessel in its place to fill it, but the jug of oil you shall not move from its place, for the Holy One, Blessed be He, is making it as a spring, and it is not customary for a spring to move from its place. I heard this Midrash Aggadah.

rashi.heb:
*הֵם מַגִּישִׁים אֵלֶיהָ.* 
הַכֵּלִים.
rashi.eng: *they were bringing to her.* the vessels.

rashi.heb:
*וַיַּעֲמֹד הַשָּׁמֶן.* 
מִלָּבֹא עוֹד, וּמִדְרַשׁ אַגָּדָה: הוֹקִיר שַׁעַר הַשֶּׁמֶן.
rashi.eng: *and the oil stopped.* coming any more. [This is the] peshat. Mid. Aggadah in Gen. Rabbah 35 explains it literally: and the oil stood up, meaning that the price of oil went up.

rashi.heb:
*וַתָּבֹא וַתַּגֵּד וְגוֹ'.* 
בָּאת לִטֹּל עֵצָה, אִם לִמְכֹּר אִם לְהַמְתִּין עַד שֶׁיּוּקַר עוֹד, אָמַר לָהּ לְכִי מִכְרִי, כִּי יֵשׁ דַּי לְכָל נִשְׁיֵךְ, וְלִחְיוֹת אַתְּ וּבָנַיִךְ בַּנּוֹתָר, עַד שֶׁיִּחְיוּ הַמֵּתִים.
rashi.eng: *And she came and told….* She came to receive advice whether to sell or to wait until it would become more expensive. He said to her, Go sell, for there is enough for all your debt, and for you and your sons to live with the remainder until the dead come to life.

notes.125: (tn): Or “she urged him to eat some food.”
notes.126: (tn): Or “he would turn aside there to eat some food.”

rashi.heb:
*וְשָׁם אִשָּׁה גְדוֹלָה.* 
חֲשׁוּבָה, וְרָאִיתִי בְּפִרְקֵי דְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר: אֲחוֹתָהּ שֶל אֲבִישַׁג הַשּׁוּנַמִּית הָיְתָה.
rashi.eng: *a prominent woman.* [lit. a great woman, i.e.,] an important woman. And I saw in Pirkei d’R. Eliezer (ch. 33): She was the sister of Abishag the Shunemitess [who warmed King David in his old age].

rashi.heb:
*וַיְהִי מִדֵּי עָבְרוֹ.* 
בְּאוֹתָהּ הָעִיר, יָסוּר אֶל בֵּיתָהּ לֶאֱכֹל לָחֶם.
rashi.eng: *and it was, whenever he would pass.* in that city, he would stop at her house to eat a meal.

rashi.heb:
*יָסֻר.* 
לְשׁוֹן הוֶֹה, הָיָה סָר שָׁם.
rashi.eng: *he would stop.* Heb. יסר, lit. he would stop. This is] the present tense, [i.e.,] he would stop there.

rashi.heb:
*הִנֵּה נָא יָדַעְתִּי.* 
שֶׁלֹּא רָאֲתָה זְבוּב עַל שֻׁלְחָנוֹ, וּקֶרִי עַל סְדִינוֹ.
rashi.eng: *Behold now I know.* For she never saw a fly on his table or semen on his sheet.

notes.129: (tn, Heb): “a small upper room of a wall”; according to HALOT 832 s.v. עֲלִיָּה, this refers to “a fully walled upper room.”
notes.130: (tn, Heb): “and let’s put there for him.”

notes.131: (tn, Heb): “he”; the referent (Elisha) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

rashi.heb:
*וַיְהִי הַיּוֹם.* 
וַיְהִי יוֹם אֶחָד.

notes.135: (tn, Heb): “and he called for her and she stood before him.”

notes.137: (tn, Heb): “you have turned trembling to us with all this trembling.” The exaggerated language is probably idiomatic. The point seems to be that she has taken great pains or gone out of her way to be kind to them. Her concern was a sign of her respect for the prophetic office.
notes.138: (tn, Heb): “Among my people I am living.” This answer suggests that she has security within the context of her family.

rashi.heb:
*חָרַדְתְּ אֵלֵינוּ.* 
בִּשְׁבִילֵנוּ.
rashi.eng: *You have busied yourself on our account.* [lit.] to us.

rashi.heb:
*אֶת כָּל הַחֲרָדָה הַזֹּאת.* 
לָשׂוּם אֶל לִבֵּךְ אֶת הָעֵסֶק הַזֶּה, כְּמוֹ: וְחָרֵד עַל דְּבָרִי, זָהִיר עַל הַדָּבָר שֶׁיְּהֵא עָשׂוּי, וְנוֹתְנוֹ אֶל לִבּוֹ.
rashi.eng: *with all this trouble.* [lit. all this shudder, i.e.] to put your heart into this task, like (Is. 66:2) “and shudders concerning My word,” [i.e.] is diligent concerning the task that it be accomplished and puts his heart into it.

rashi.heb:
*מֶה לַעֲשׂוֹת לָךְ.* 
מָה אַתְּ צְרִיכָה שֶׁנַּעֲשֶׂה לָךְ, שֶׁבִּשְׁבִילֵנוּ עָסַקְתְּ כָּל זֶה.
rashi.eng: *What is there to do for you?.* What do you need that we do for you, for you busied yourself with all this for us.

rashi.heb:
*בְּתוֹךְ עַמִּי.* 
בְּתוֹךְ קְרוֹבַי, אֵין אָדָם מַזִּיקֵנִי, אֵינִי צְרִיכָה לְמֶלֶךְ וְלֹא לְשַׂר הַצָּבָא.
rashi.eng: *“I dwell in the midst of my people.”.* amidst my relatives. No one harms me. I have need neither for the King nor for the general of the army.

rashi.heb:
*וַיֹּאמֶר אֱלִישָׁע.* 
לְגֵיחֲזִי.
rashi.eng: *And he said.* Elisha to Gehazi.

rashi.heb:
*וּמֶה לַעֲשׂוֹת לָהּ.* 
נֶגֶד הַטּוֹבָה הַזֹּאת.
rashi.eng: *“Now what can we do for her?”.* to reciprocate for this favor.

notes.142: (tn, Heb): “and he called for her and she stood in the door.”

notes.143: (tn, Heb): “at this appointed time, at the time [when it is] reviving.” For a discussion of the second phrase see M. Cogan and H. Tadmor, II Kings (AB), 57.

rashi.heb:
*לַמּוֹעֵד הַזֶּה.* 
כָּעֵת חַיָּה. כְּמוֹ שֶׁאַתְּ קַיֶּמֶת הַיּוֹם וּלְשָׁלוֹם, כָּךְ תְּהִי קַיֶּמֶת לַמּוֹעֵד הַזֶּה, וְחוֹבֶקֶת בֵּן.
rashi.eng: *At this time next year when you will be alive like now.* [lit. like the time, alive, i.e.] just as you are alive today, and well, so will you be alive next year at this time and embracing a son.

rashi.heb:
*אַל אֲדֹנִי.* 
אַל תֹּאמַר חוֹבֶקֶת בֵּן, מַה לִּי חִבּוּקוֹ אִם סוֹפִי לְקָבְרוֹ, וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרָה לּוֹ כְּשֶׁמֵּת הֲלֹא אָמַרְתִּי לֹא תַשְׁלֶה אוֹתִי.
rashi.eng: *No, my lord.* Do not say, “embracing a son.” Why do I need to embrace him if I will end up burying him? This is what she said to him when he died, “Did I not say, ‘Do not mislead me?’”

rashi.heb:
*אַל תְּכַזֵּב.* 
אַל תַּרְאֵנִי דָּבָר שֶׁיִּפְסֹק, יֵשׁ בְּיָדְךָ לְבַקֵּשׁ רַחֲמִים וְיִנָּתֵן לִי בֵּן, אַךְ בְּבַקָּשָׁה מִמְּךָ אַל תִּתֵּן לִי אֶלָּא בֵּן שֶל קַיָּמָא.
rashi.eng: *do not fail.* Do not show me something that will fail. You have power to beg mercy, and a son will be given to me. I beseech you, do not give me any but a child who will live.

rashi.heb:
*אַל תְּכַזֵּב.* 
כְּמוֹ: לֹא יְכַזְּבוּ מֵימָיו.
rashi.eng: *do not fail.* like (Is. 58:11) “whose water will not fail.”

rashi.heb:
*כָּעֵת חַיָּה.* 
כָּעֵת הַזֹּאת שֶׁהָיְתָה בְחַיִּים וּבְשָׁלוֹם, וּלְכָךְ נָקוּד כָּעֵת.
rashi.eng: *at this time a year later.* like this time that she was alive and well. Therefore, the word is voweled כָּעֵת; [i.e., like] the [time].

notes.144: (tn, Heb): “to his father, to the harvesters.”

notes.145: (tn, Heb): “He”; the referent (the boy’s father) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

rashi.heb:
*רֹאשִׁי רֹאשִׁי.* 
הִנְנִי חוֹלֶה בְּרֹאשִׁי.
rashi.eng: *My head! My head!.* I am sick in my head!

rashi.heb:
*וַיֹּאמֶר.* 
אָבִיו אֶל אֶחָד מִן הַנְּעָרִים, שָׂאֵהוּ אֶל אִמּוֹ.
rashi.eng: *And he said.* His father [said] to one of the servants, “Carry him to his mother” .

notes.148: (sn): The new moon was a time of sacrifice and special feasts (Num 28:14; 1 Sam 20:5). Apparently it was a convenient time to visit a prophet. See M. Cogan and H. Tadmor, II Kings (AB), 57.

notes.151: (tn, Heb): “do not restrain for me the riding unless I say to you.”

rashi.heb: *נְהַג וָלֵךְ.* מַהֵר.
rashi.eng: *Drive and go forward.* quickly.

rashi.heb: *אַל תַּעֲצָר לִי.* אַל תְּעַכֵּב עַל יָדִי אֶת הָרְכִיבָה.
rashi.eng: *Don’t keep back from riding because of me.* Do not keep back the riding because of me.

notes.153: (tn, Heb): “the man of God.” The phrase has been replaced by the relative pronoun “he” in the translation for stylistic reasons.

notes.154: (tn, Heb): “she said.” The narrator streamlines the story at this point, omitting any reference to Gehazi running to meet her and asking her the questions.

rashi.heb:
*וַתֹּאמֶר שָׁלוֹם.* 
הֲרֵי זֶה מִקְרָא קָצָר, שֶׁהֲרֵי הָיָה לוֹ לִכְתֹּב, וַיִּשְׁאַל לָהּ וַתֹּאמֶר שָׁלוֹם.
rashi.eng: *And she said, “We are well.”.* This is an abbreviated verse, So he should have written, “And he asked her, and she said, We are well.”

rashi.heb:
*הֲלֹא אָמַרְתִּי.* 
לְךָ, אַל תְּכַזֵּב בְּשִׁפְחָתֶךָ.
rashi.eng: *Did I not say.* to you, Do not fail your maidservant?

rashi.heb:
*לֹא תַשְׁלֶה.* 
לֹא תַשְׁגֶּה אוֹתִי עַל דְּבַר טָעוּת.
rashi.eng: *'Do not mislead me?'.* Do not mislead me concerning a mistaken thing.

notes.156: (tn, Heb): “he”; the referent (Elisha) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
notes.157: (tn, Heb): “take my staff in your hand.”
notes.158: (tn, Heb): “If you meet a man, do not greet him with a blessing; if a man greets you with a blessing, do not answer.”

rashi.heb:
*לֹא תְבָרְכֶנּוּ.* 
לֹא תִּשְׁאַל לְשָׁלוֹם, וְכָל זֶה שֶׁלֹּא יַרְבֶּה דְבָרִים וְיִשְׁאָלֵהוּ לְהֵיכָן אַתָּה הוֹלֵךְ, וְהוּא אוֹמֵר לְהַחֲיוֹת אֶת הַמֵּת, וְאֵין זֶה כְּבוֹד הַנֵּס לְהִתְהַלֵּל בּוֹ מִי שֶׁבָּא עַל יָדוֹ. וְהוּא לֹא עָשָׂה כֵּן, אֶלָּא לְכָל הַשּׁוֹאֲלוֹ הוּא אוֹמֵר רַבִּי שְׁלָחַנִי לְהַחֲיוֹת אֶת הַמֵּת.
rashi.eng: *do not greet him.* [lit. do not bless him.] Do not ask him about his welfare. All this was done so that he would not be engaged in conversation, and he would ask him, “Where are you going?” And he would say, “To revive the dead.” Now, it is not respectful for the one through whom it is coming about, to praise himself. He, however, did not do so. Instead, to every inquirer he would say, “My master sent me to revive the dead.”

notes.159: (tn, Heb): “he”; the referent (Elisha) has been specified in the translation for clarity. The referent must be Elisha here, since the following verse makes it clear that Gehazi had gone on ahead of them.

notes.162: (tn, Heb): “and closed the door behind the two of them.”

notes.163: (tn, Heb): “he went up and lay down over.”
notes.164: (tn, Heb): “his” (also in the next two clauses).

rashi.heb:
*וַיִּגְהַר עָלָיו.* 
תִּרְגֵּם יוֹנָתָן: וְאַלְהֵי עֲלוֹהִי, הוּא לְשׁוֹן עֲיֵפוּת, יֵשׁ דֻּגְמָתוֹ בְּבָרַיְיתָא דְּהַאֲזִינוּ וּבְסִפְרִי. וּמְנַחֵם פָּתַר: 'וַיִּגְהַר' פִּתְרוֹן הַמִּלָּה כְּפִי עִנְיָנָהּ, נִשְׁתַּטַּח עָלָיו.
rashi.eng: *and he prostrated himself upon him.* Jonathan renders: וְאַלְהֵי עֲלוֹהִי This is an expression of weariness. [I.e., he lay exhausted upon him.] There is a similar word in the Baraitha of Haazinu and in Sifrei (references obscure). And Menahem interpreted [as follows]: The interpretation of the word according to its context, is: he prostrated himself upon him.

notes.166: (tn, Heb): “he”; the referent (Elisha) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
notes.167: (tn, Heb): “and he returned and went into the house, once here and once there.”

rashi.heb:
*וַיְזוֹרֵר.* 
נִתְעַטֵּשׁ.

notes.169: (tn, Heb): “he”; the referent (Elisha) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

notes.171: (tn, Heb): “the sons of the prophets were sitting before him.”
notes.172: (tn): The words “the fire” are added for clarification.

rashi.heb:
*שְׁפֹת הַסִּיר.* 
הוֹשִׁיבָהּ עַל הַכִּירָה.
rashi.eng: *set the… pot.* Place it on the stove

rashi.heb:
*נָזִיד.* 
תַּבְשִׁיל.
rashi.eng: *a stew.* Heb. נָזִיד, a cooked dish.

rashi.heb:
*לִבְנֵי הַנְּבִיאִים.* 
לְתַלְמִידֵי נְבִיַּיָּא.

notes.175: (tn, Heb): “[some] of the gourds of the field.”
notes.177: (tc): The Hebrew text reads, “for they did not know” (יָדָעוּ, yada’u) but some emend the final shureq (וּ, indicating a third plural subject) to holem vav (וֹ, a third masculine singular pronominal suffix on a third singular verb) and read “for he did not know it.” Perhaps it is best to omit the final vav as dittographic (note the vav at the beginning of the next verb form) and read simply, “for he did not know.” See M. Cogan and H. Tadmor, II Kings (AB), 59.

rashi.heb:
*לְלַקֵּט אֹרֹת.* 
גַּרְגִּיר שֶׁקּוֹרִין אוֹרְגָּא, שֶׁמֵּאִיר אֶת הָעֵינַיִם. וְיֵשׁ שֶׁפּוֹתְרִין 'אֹרֹת' יְרָקוֹת, כְּמוֹ: כְּחֹם צַח עֲלֵי אוֹר.
rashi.eng: *to gather herbs.* [Heb.] oroth, garden rocket, which they call eruca [in Latin], which brightens the eyes, meir [in Heb.] (Yoma 18b). Others interpret ‘oroth’ as herbs, as (Is. 18: 4) “Like a clear heat on herbs (‘or’).”

rashi.heb:
*וַיִּמְצָא גֶּפֶן שָׂדֶה.* 
גּוּפְנָא בְּחַקְלָא.
rashi.eng: *a vine in the field.* This follows Jonathan.

rashi.heb:
*וַיְלַקֵּט מִמֶּנּוּ פַּקֻּעֹת שָׂדֶה.* 
צָמְחוּ מִמֶּנּוּ פַּקּוּעוֹת שָׂדֶה, הוּא בוליי"ן בְּלַעַ"ז, סַם הַמָּוֶת. וּבְשֵׁם רַבִּי מְנַחֵם שָׁמַעְתִּי: וַיְלַקֵּט לְבַד מִמֶּנּוּ, בִּלְעָדָיו, פַּקּוּעוֹת שָׂדֶה.
rashi.eng: *and gathered from it wild mushrooms.* Wild mushrooms grew from it. That is boljic in O.F: It is poisonous. [It is common that mushrooms grow from old tree stumps and the like. In this case, they grew from a vine.] And in the name of Rabbi Menahem. I heard, and he gathered in addition to the fruit that grew from it, wild mushrooms.

rashi.heb:
*וַיְפַלַּח.* 
וַיְבַקַּע.
rashi.eng: *and diced them.* split them.

notes.178: (tn, Heb): “and they poured out [the stew].” The plural subject is probably indefinite.

notes.181: (tn): On the meaning of the word צִקְלוֹן (tsiqlon), “ear of grain,” see HALOT 148 s.v. בָּצֵק and M. Cogan and H. Tadmor, II Kings (AB), 59.
notes.182: (tn, Heb): “he”; the referent (Elisha) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

rashi.heb:
*מִבַּעַל שָׁלִשָׁה.* 
שֵׁם מְדִינָה. וְיוֹנָתָן תִּרְגֵּם: מֵאַרְעָא דָּרוֹמָא. 'בַּעַל' לְשׁוֹן 'מִישׁוֹר', וְהַרְבֵּה בַּמִּקְרָא.
rashi.eng: *from Baal Shalishah.* the name of a province. And Jonathan rendered: from the southland. “Baal” is an expression meaning a plain. There are many such expressions in the Bible.

rashi.heb:
*לֶחֶם בִּכּוּרִים.* 
בְּפֶסַח, שֶׁהַתְּבוּאָה מְבַכֶּרֶת.
rashi.eng: *bread of the first fruits.* It was during Passover, when the grain becomes ripe.

rashi.heb:
*בְּצִקְלֹנוֹ.* 
בִּלְבוּשֵׁיהּ.
rashi.eng: *in their shells.* Jonathan [renders]: in their garments. [The shell is compared to a garment of the grain].

rashi.heb:
*לָעָם.* 
לַתַּלְמִידִים שֶׁהָיָה זָן.
rashi.eng: *to the people.* to the students whom he sustained.

notes.183: (tn, Heb): “How can I set this before a hundred men?”
notes.184: (tn, Heb): The verb forms are infinitives absolute ( “eating and leaving over”) and have to be translated in light of the context.

rashi.heb:
*מַה אֶתֵּן זֶה.* 
כָּל לֶחֶם וְלֶחֶם.
rashi.eng: *How will I give this.* [i.e.,] each bread.

notes.185: (tn, Heb): “according to the word of the Lord.”

notes.186: (tn, Heb): “was a great man before his master and lifted up with respect to the face.”
notes.187: (tn): For a discussion of מְצֹרָע (m�tsora’), traditionally translated “leprous,” see M. Cogan and H. Tadmor, II Kings (AB), 63. Naaman probably had a skin disorder of some type, not leprosy/Hansen’s disease.

rashi.heb:
*וְנַעֲמָן שַׂר צְבָא.* 
נִסִּים שֶׁנַּעֲשׂוּ עַל יְדֵי אֱלִישָׁע, מְסַדֵּר וְהוֹלֵךְ.
rashi.eng: *Now, Naaman the general.* He goes on to recount the miracles that were performed through Elisha.

rashi.heb:
*תְּשׁוּעָה לַאֲרָם.* 
הוּא מָשַׁךְ בַּקֶּשֶׁת לְתֻמּוֹ, וְהָרַג אֶת אַחְאָב.
rashi.eng: *the victory to Aram.* He drew back his bow innocently and killed Ahab.

rashi.heb:
*יָצְאוּ גְדוּדִים.* 
כְּשֶׁהוֹלְכִין מֵאָה אוֹ מָאתַיִם מֵעַצְמָן לִשְׁלֹל כַּאֲשֶׁר יִמְצְאוּן, הוּא קָרוּי גְּדוּד.
rashi.eng: *went out in bands.* When they go in groups of one hundred or two hundred by themselves, to plunder whatever they find, that is called a band.

rashi.heb:
*נַעֲרָה קְטַנָּה.* 
רִיבָה קְטַנָּה, מֵעִיר נַעֲרוֹן.
rashi.eng: *a young girl.* Heb. naarah ketannah, a young girl from the town of Naaran.

rashi.heb:
*וַתְּהִי לִפְנֵי.* 
וַהֲוַת מְשַׁמְּשָׁא קֳדָם אִתַּת נַעֲמָן.
rashi.eng: *who ministered to.* [lit. and she was before Naaman’s wife.] Jonathan [renders]: and she was serving before Naaman’s wife.

notes.188: (map): For location see Map2-B1; Map4-D3; Map5-E2; Map6-A4; Map7-C1.

rashi.heb:
*אַחֲלֵי אֲדֹנִי.* 
לִפְנֵי הַנָּבִיא. לְשׁוֹן וַיְחַל משֶׁה, בַּקָּשׁוֹת כָּל הַמִּתְפַּלְּלִים עָלָיו יִהְיוּ, שֶׁיָּבוֹא הַנֵּס לִפְנֵי הַנָּבִיא.
rashi.eng: *My master’s supplications.* before the prophet Heb. אֲחֲלֵי, an expression similar to וַיְחַל מֹשֶה, “and Moses prayed” (Ex. 32:11). The supplications of all those who pray for him, shall be that the miracle shall come before the prophet.

rashi.heb:
*אַחֲלֵי.* 
שוהיידמנ"ס בְּלַעַ"ז, כְּלוֹמַר זוֹ הִיא בַּקָּשָׁה שֶׁהוּא צָרִיךְ לָהּ.
rashi.eng: *the supplications.* אַחֲלֵי I.e., to say that this is the supplication that he requires.

notes.189: (tn, Heb): “he”; the referent (Naaman) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

rashi.heb:
*וַיָּבֹא.* 
נַעֲמָן.
rashi.eng: *And he came.* [i.e.,] Naaman [came]

rashi.heb:
*וַיַּגֵּד לַאדֹנָיו.* 
מֶלֶךְ אֲרָם.
rashi.eng: *and told his master.* the king of Aram.

notes.190: (tn, Heb): “he”; the referent (Naaman) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
notes.191: (tn): The Hebrew term כִּכָּר (kikkar, “circle”) refers generally to something that is round. When used of metals it can refer to a disk-shaped weight made of the metal or to a standard unit of weight, generally regarded as a talent. Since the accepted weight for a talent of metal is about 75 pounds, this would have amounted to about 750 pounds of silver (cf. NCV, NLT, CEV).
notes.192: (tn, Heb): “six thousand gold […].” The unit of measure is not given in the Hebrew text. A number of English versions supply “pieces” (e.g., KJV, ASV, NAB, TEV) or “shekels” (e.g., NASB, NIV, NRSV).

rashi.heb:
*וַיִּקַּח בְּיָדוֹ.* 
מִנְחָה לַנָּבִיא.
rashi.eng: *and he took in his possession.* as a gift to the prophet.

rashi.heb:
*וְשֵׁשֶׁת אֲלָפִים זָהָב.* 
זְהוּבִים.
rashi.eng: *and six thousand gold pieces.* [lit.] and six thousand gold.

notes.193: (tn, Heb): “and now when this letter comes to you, look, I have sent to you Naaman my servant.”

rashi.heb:
*לֵאמֹר וְעַתָּה כְּבוֹא הַסֵּפֶר הַזֶּה וְגוֹ'.* 
הַסֵּפֶר אָמַר לוֹ, וְעַתָּה כְּבוֹא הַסֵּפֶר הַזֶּה וְגוֹ'.
rashi.eng: *saying.* [“And now when this letter comes…5”]-The letter said to him, “And now, when this letter…”

rashi.heb:
*וַאֲסַפְתּוֹ מִצָּרַעְתּוֹ.* 
'אֲסֵפָה' בִּמְצֹרָע הִיא לְשׁוֹן רְפוּאָתוֹ, כִּי בְּהִתְרַפּאוֹתוֹ הוּא נֶאֱסָף אֶל תּוֹךְ בְּנֵי אָדָם, וּבְחָלְיוֹ הַכֹּל בְּדֵלִין הֵימֶנּוּ.
rashi.eng: *and you shall cure him of his zaraath.* [lit. and you shall gather him in from his zaraath.] Gathering, as applied to the mezora, is the expression of his cure, for when he is cured, he is gathered in among people, whereas during his illness, everyone stays away from him.

notes.194: (tn, Heb): “Am I God, killing and restoring life, that this one sends to me to cure a man from his skin disease?” In the Hebrew text this is one lengthy rhetorical question, which has been divided up in the translation for stylistic reasons.
notes.195: (tn, Heb): “Indeed, know and see that he is seeking an occasion with respect to me.”

rashi.heb:
*הַאֱלֹהִים אָנִי.* 
הֵ"א נָקוּד פַּתָּ"ח, לְלַמֵּד שֶׁהוּא בִּלְשׁוֹן תְּמִיהָה.
rashi.eng: *Do I have power from God.* [after] Jonathan. [Lit. Am I God?] The ‘heh’ at the beginning of the word הַאֱלֹהִים, is voweled with a ‘pathah’ to indicate that it is a question.

rashi.heb:
*מִתְאַנֶּה.* 
מְבַקֵּשׁ תּוֹאֲנָה לְהִתְגָּרוֹת בִּי.
rashi.eng: *he is looking for a pretext.* He is looking for a pretext to engage in strife with me.

rashi.heb:
*מִתְאַנֶּה.* 
לְשׁוֹן עֲלִילוֹת דְּבָרִים.
rashi.eng: *he is looking for a pretext.*  [Heb. מִתְאַנֶה] an expression of pretext.

rashi.heb:
*הִנֵּה אָמַרְתִּי.* 
סָבוּר הָיִיתִי, אֵלַי יֵצֵא הַנָּבִיא וִידַבֵּר עִמִּי וְיִרְאֶה אֶת הַחֹלִי.
rashi.eng: *Here I thought.* [I thought that] the prophet would come out and speak with me, and see the ailment.

rashi.heb:
*וְהֵנִיף יָדוֹ אֶל הַמָּקוֹם.* 
הַצָּרַעַת.
rashi.eng: *and he would raise his hand toward the spot.* of the] zaraath.

notes.199: (tn, Heb): “Are not Abana and Pharpar, the rivers of Damascus, better than all of the waters of Israel?” The rhetorical question expects an emphatic “yes” as an answer.

notes.200: (tn, Heb): “my father,” reflecting the perspective of each individual servant. To address their master as “father” would emphasize his authority and express their respect. See BDB 3 s.v. אָב and the similar idiomatic use of “father” in 2 Kgs 2:12.
notes.202: (tn, Heb): “would you not do [it]?” The rhetorical question expects the answer, “Of course you would.”
notes.203: (tn, Heb): “How much more [when] he said, “Wash and be healed.” The second imperative (“be healed”) states the expected result of obeying the first (‘wash”).

rashi.heb:
*אָבִי.* 
כְּמוֹ אֲדוֹנִי.
rashi.eng: *Master.* [lit. father].

rashi.heb:
*הֲלוֹא תַעֲשֶׂה.* 
וְכִי לֹא תַעֲשֵׂהוּ, אֲפִלּוּ אָמַר לְךָ דְּבַר טֹרַח.
rashi.eng: *would you not do it?.* Would you not do it even if he ordered you to do something requiring exertion?

rashi.heb:
*וְאַף כִּי.* 
קַל וָחֹמֶר שֶׁאָמַר לְךָ דָּבָר קַל, רְחַץ וּטְהָר.
rashi.eng: *and surely.* by a fortiori conclusion, since he said to you to do an easy thing, [viz.] immerse yourself and become clean.

notes.204: (tn, Heb): “according to the word of the man of God.”
notes.205: (tn, Heb): “and his skin was restored, like the skin of a small child.”

notes.206: (tn, Heb): “he”; the referent (Naaman) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

rashi.heb:
*בְרָכָה.* 
מִנְחַת שָׁלוֹם שֶל הַקְבָּלַת פָּנִים, שֶׁשּׁוֹאֵל תַּלְמִיד אוֹ עֶבֶד בִּשְׁלוֹם הָרַב, שולד"ו בְּלַעַ"ז.
rashi.eng: *a gift.* [lit. a blessing], a gift of peace, of greeting, when a disciple or a slave greets his master (sallud in O.F., a greeting).

notes.208: (tn, Heb): “he”; the referent (Elisha) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
notes.210: (tn, Heb): “he”; the referent (Naaman) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

rashi.heb:
*אִם אֶקָּח.* 
שֶׁדְּמֵי עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה מְעֹרָבִין בּוֹ.
rashi.eng: *I will not accept.* for the price of idols was included in it.

notes.211: (tn, Heb): “and [if] not, may there be given to your servant a load [for] a pair of mules, earth.”
notes.212: (tn, Heb): “for your servant will not again make a burnt offering and sacrifice to other gods, only to the Lord.”

rashi.heb:
*וָלֹא.* 
לְשׁוֹן בַּקָּשָׁה, לְשׁוֹן הַלְוַאי.
rashi.eng: *Now, if only.* וָלֹא, an expression of a request, an expression of הַלְוַאי.

rashi.heb:
*יֻתַּן נָא.* 
מֵאֲדָמָה זוֹ מֵאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁהִיא קְדוֹשָׁה, מַשָּׂא שְׁנֵי פְּרָדִים, וְאֶשָּׂאֶנָּה לְעִירִי וְאֶעֱשֶׂה אוֹתָהּ מִזְבֵּחַ.
rashi.eng: *Now… be given.* from this soil of the land of Israel, which is holy, a load of earth as carried by a team of mules, and I will carry it off to my city, and I will make it into an altar.

notes.213: (tn, Heb): “When my master enters the house of Rimmon to bow down there, and he leans on my hand and I bow down [in] the house of Rimmon, when I bow down [in] the house of Rimmon, may the Lord forgive your servant for this thing.” Rimmon was the Syrian storm god. See M. Cogan and H. Tadmor, II Kings (AB), 65.

rashi.heb:
*בֵית רִמּוֹן.* 
שֵׁם עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה.
rashi.eng: *Beth-Rimmon.* the name of a pagan deity.

rashi.heb:
*וְהִשְׁתַּחֲוֵיתִי.* 
עַל כָּרְחִי, כְּשֶׁשּׁוֹחֶה אֲדוֹנִי וְהוּא נִשְׁעָן עַל יָדִי.
rashi.eng: *and I will prostrate myself.* against my will when my master bows, since he leans on my hand.

notes.214: (tn, Heb): “he”; the referent (Elisha) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
notes.215: (tn, Heb): “and he went from him a distance of land.” The precise meaning of כִּבְרַה (kivrah) “distance,” is uncertain. See BDB 460 s.v. כִּבְרַה, and HALOT 459-60 s.v. II *כְּבָרַה, and M. Cogan and H. Tadmor, II Kings (AB), 65.

rashi.heb:
*כִּבְרַת אָרֶץ.* 
שֵׁם מִדָּה שֶל קַרְקַע, כְּמוֹ: צִמְדֵי כֶרֶם, ארפינ"ט בְּלַעַ"ז.
rashi.eng: *some distance.* [Heb.] kivrath eretz, the name of a land measure, like (Is. 5:10) “ten acres of vineyard.” (arpent in French), an old French measure of land, equivalent to about an acre.

notes.217: (tn, Heb): “Look, my master spared this Syrian Naaman by not taking from his hand what he brought.”

rashi.heb:
*מְאוּמָה.* 
חָסֵר אָלֶ"ף, לְפִי שֶׁהָיְתָה לְקִיחָה זוֹ לְמוּם.
rashi.eng: *something.* Heb. מאומה The “aleph” is missing, since this taking was responsible for his being stricken with a blemish. מוּם [in Heb.].

rashi.heb:
*וַיִּפֹּל.* 
וְאִתְרְכִין.
rashi.eng: *and he leaned over.* Jonathan. [Lit. and he fell.]

notes.220: (tn, Heb): “Look now, here, two servants came to me from the Ephraimite hill country, from the sons of the prophets.”
notes.221: (tn): The Hebrew term כִּכָּר (kikkar, “circle”) refers generally to something that is round. When used of metals it can refer to a disk-shaped weight made of the metal or to a standard unit of weight, generally regarded as a talent. Since the accepted weight for a talent of metal is about 75 pounds, this would have amounted to about 75 pounds of silver (cf. NCV, NLT, CEV).

notes.222: (tn, Heb): “Be resolved and accept two talents.”

rashi.heb:
*הוֹאֵל.* 
הִשָּׁבַע שֶׁשְּׁלַחֲךָ.
rashi.eng: *Please.* swear that he sent you.

rashi.heb:
*בִּשְׁנֵי חֲרִטִים.* 
מִינֵי בְּגָדִים וְסוּדָרִין, כְּמוֹ: הַמִּטְפָּחוֹת וְהָחֲרִיטִים, כָּךְ חִבְּרוֹ מְנַחֵם. אֲבָל יוֹנָתָן תִּרְגֵּם זֶה 'פַּלְדָּסִין', וְאֶת שֶׁבְּסֵפֶר יְשַׁעְיָהוּ תִּרְגֵּם 'מְחַכַּיָּא'. וְהַפּוֹתְרִין אוֹמְרִין: בִּשְׁנֵי חֲרִיטֵי, בִּשְׁנֵי כִּיסִין אֲרֻכִּים, פירדיי"ש בְּלַעַ"ז.
rashi.eng: *in two pockets.* Heb. חֲרִטִים types of garments and kerchiefs, like (Is. 3:22) “and the kerchiefs and the ‘haritim.’” Menahem classified it thus (p. 94). Jonathan, however, translated this as ‘paldesin,’ sheets, (see Targum Jud. 14) and the one in the book of Isaiah as ‘mahachaia,’ a plate covering the genitals. The exegetes say that בִּשְׁנֵי חֲרִטִים, [means] ‘in two long pockets’ brids in O.F.

rashi.heb:
*אֶל שְׁנֵי נְעָרָיו.* 
שֶׁל נַעֲמָן.
rashi.eng: *his two servants.* [i.e.,] Naaman’s.

rashi.heb:
*וַיִּשְׂאוּ לְפָנָיו.* 
לִפְנֵי גֵּחֲזִי.
rashi.eng: *and they carried them before him.* before Gehazi.

notes.225: (tn, Heb): “and he sent the men away and they went.”

rashi.heb:
*וַיָּבֹא אֶל הָעֹפֶל.* 
תִּרְגֵּם יוֹנָתָן: לַאֲתַר כָּסֵי.
rashi.eng: *And he came to a secret place.* Jonathan renders: to a hidden place.

rashi.heb:
*וַיִּקַּח מִיָּדָם.* 
מִיַּד שְׁנֵי נַעֲרֵי נַעֲמָן.
rashi.eng: *and he took them from their hands.* from the hands of Naaman’s two servants.

rashi.heb:
*וַיְשַׁלַּח אֶת הָאֲנָשִׁים.* 
שֶׁלֹּא יִרְאֶה אוֹתָם אֱלִישָׁע.
rashi.eng: *and he dismissed the men.* lest Elisha see them.

notes.226: (tn, Heb): “he”; the referent (Elisha) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
notes.227: (tn, Heb): “Did not my heart go as a man turned from his chariot to meet you?” The rhetorical question emphasizes that he was indeed present in “heart” (or “spirit”) and was very much aware of what Gehazi had done. In the MT the interrogative particle has been accidentally omitted before the negative particle.
notes.228: (tn): In the MT the statement is phrased as a rhetorical question, “Is this the time…?” It expects an emphatic negative response.

rashi.heb:
*הַעֵת לָקַחַת אֶת הַכֶּסֶף.* 
לְהִתְעַשֵּׁר, וְלָקַחַת מִמֶּנּוּ בְּגָדִים וְזֵיתִים וְגוֹ'.
rashi.eng: *Is it time to take the silver.* to become wealthy and to buy with it clothing and olive trees…

notes.230: (tn, Heb): “he”; the referent (Gehazi) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
notes.231: (tn): Traditionally, “he went from before him, leprous like snow.” But see the note at 5:1, as well as M. Cogan and H. Tadmor, II Kings (AB), 66.

rashi.heb:
*וַיֹּאמְרוּ בְנֵי הַנְּבִיאִים.* 
נִסִּים שֶׁנַּעֲשׂוּ לוֹ מְסַדֵּר וְהוֹלֵךְ. רַבּוֹתֵינוּ אָמְרוּ: מִכָּאן שֶׁהָיָה גֵּיחֲזִי דּוֹחֶה הַתַּלְמִידִים מִלְּפָנָיו, וּכְשֶׁנִּטְרַד בָּאוּ תַּלְמִידִים רַבִּים, וְנִדְחַק הַמָּקוֹם מֵהֶם.
rashi.eng: *And the disciples of the prophets said.* He continues to enumerate the miracles that were performed for him (sic). Our Sages deduced from here that Gehazi would reject the pupils from before him, and when he was banished, many pupils came, and the place became too cramped for them.

rashi.heb:
*הוֹאֶל.* 
הִתְרַצֶּה.
rashi.eng: *be willing.* Heb. הואל.

rashi.heb:
*וְאֶת הַבַּרְזֶל.* 
הַנְּסֹרֶת.

*וְהוּא שָׁאוּל.* 
שְׁאִלְתִּיו, וְאֵין לִי מִמַּה לְשַׁלֵּם.
rashi.eng: *it is borrowed.* I borrowed it, and I have not the wherewithal to pay.

notes.238: (tn, Heb): “he”; the referent (Elisha) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

rashi.heb:
*וַיָּצֶף.* 
צָף עַל הַמַּיִם.
rashi.eng: *floated.* floated on the water.

notes.239: (tc): The verb form used here is difficult to analyze. On the basis of the form נְחִתִּים (n�khitim) in v. 9 from the root נָחַת (nakhat), it is probably best to emend the verb to תִּנְחְתוּ (tinkh�tu; a Qal imperfect form from the same root). The verb נָחַת in at least two other instances carries the nuance “go down, descend” in a military context. For a defense of this view, see M. Cogan and H. Tadmor, II Kings (AB), 72.
notes.240: (sn): The advisers would have mentioned a specific location, but the details are not significant to the narrator’s purpose, so he simply paraphrases here.

rashi.heb:
*פְּלֹנִי אַלְמֹנִי.* 
כָּסֵי וְטָמִיר, פְּלוֹנִי, לְשׁוֹן: כִּי יִפָּלֵא 'יִתְכַּסֵּי'.
rashi.eng: *hidden, secret.* Jonathan [renders]: covered and hidden. פְּלֹנִי is an expression of (Deut. 17:8) “If it be concealed” (יִפָּלֵא).

rashi.heb:
*אַלְמוֹנִי.* 
מִבְּלִי שֵׁם, שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה רוֹצֶה לְהִתְגַּלּוֹת.
rashi.eng: *secret.* without a name, for he did not want it to be revealed.

rashi.heb:
*תַּחֲנֹתִי.* 
שָׁם אֶחֱנֶה, וְאֶאֱרֹב אֶת מֶלֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵל אוֹ אֶת גְּדוּדָיו הָעוֹבְרִים לִשְׁלֹל בְּאַרְצִי דֶּרֶךְ אוֹתוֹ הַמָּקוֹם.
rashi.eng: *I will encamp.* There I will encamp and ambush the king of Israel or his bands who pass to plunder in my land through that place.

rashi.heb:
*מֵעֲבֹר הַמָּקוֹם הַזֶּה.* 
מִלֶּכֶת שָׁם.
rashi.eng: *of passing this place.* [i.e.,] from going there.

rashi.heb:
*נְחִתִּים.* 
חוֹנִים.
rashi.eng: *are encamped.* Heb. נְחִתִּים.

notes.241: (tn): The vav + perfect here indicates action contemporary with the preceding main verb (“sent”). See IBHS 533-34 �32.2.3e.
notes.242: (tn, Heb): “and the king of Israel sent to the place about which the man of God spoke to him, and he warned it and he guarded himself there, not once and not twice.”

rashi.heb:
*וַיִּשְׁלַח מֶלֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵל.* 
הָיָה שׁוֹלֵחַ וְרוֹאֶה אִם אֱמֶת הוּא.
rashi.eng: *And the king of Israel sent.* He would send and see whether it was true.

rashi.heb:
*וְהִזְהִירֹה.* 
שֶׁהִזְהִיר אִישׁ הָאֱלֹהִים מֵעֲבֹר שָׁם.
rashi.eng: *and cautioned him.* concerning which the man of God had cautioned him from passing.

rashi.heb:
*לֹא אַחַת וְלֹא שְׁתָּיִם.* 
עָשָׂה לוֹ כָּךְ, כִּי אִם פְּעָמִים רַבּוֹת.
rashi.eng: *not once and not twice.* did he do so for him, but many times.

notes.243: (tn, Heb): “and the heart of the king of Syria was stirred up over this thing.”
notes.245: (tn, Heb): “Will you not tell me who among us [is] for the king of Israel?” The sarcastic rhetorical question expresses the king’s suspicion.

rashi.heb:
*עַל הַדָּבָר הַזֶּה.* 
מִי הוּא מְגַלֶּה סוֹדוֹ.
rashi.eng: *about this matter.* who was revealing his secret.

notes.246: (tn, Heb): “he” (also a second time in this verse); the referent (the king) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
notes.247: (tn, Heb): “Go and see where he [is] so I can send and take him.”

rashi.heb:
*אֵיכֹה.* 
הֵיכָן הוּא.
rashi.eng: *where he is.* where he is.

notes.250: (tn, Heb): “his young servant said to him.”

notes.251: (tn, Heb): “for those who are with us are more than those who are with them.”

rashi.heb:
*אֲשֶׁר אִתָּנוּ.* 
בְּעֶזְרָתֵנוּ.
rashi.eng: *who are with us.* [i.e.,] who are on our side (helping us).

notes.253: (tn, Heb): “and they came down to him.”
notes.254: (tn): Or “this nation,” perhaps emphasizing the strength of the Syrian army.
notes.255: (tn): On the basis of the Akkadian etymology of the word, M. Cogan and H. Tadmor (II Kings [AB], 74) translate “blinding light.” HALOT 761 s.v. סַנְוֵרִים suggests the glosses “dazzling, deception.”
notes.256: (tn, Heb): “he”; the referent (the Lord) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
notes.257: (tn, Heb): “according to the word of Elisha.”

rashi.heb:
*וַיֹּאמַר הַךְ נָא וְגוֹ'.* 
עַל הַקְּלָלָה לֹא הִזְכִּיר אֶת הַשֵּׁם, אֲבָל עַל הַפְּקִיחָה הִזְכִּיר אֶת הַשֵּׁם עַל שְׁתֵּיהֶן, עַל שֶל נַעַר וְעַל שֶל גְּדוּד.
rashi.eng: *and said, Please strike….* On the curse he did not mention the Name [of God,] but on opening the eyes he mentioned the Name [of God] on both of them, concerning [opening] the attendant’s [eyes], and concerning [opening the eyes] of the troop.

rashi.heb:
*סַנְוֵרִים.* 
חֹלִי שֶׁל שִׁמָּמוֹן, רוֹאֶה וְאֵינוֹ יוֹדֵעַ מַה הוּא רוֹאֶה.
rashi.eng: *with blindness.* a sickness of confusion; one sees, yet does not know what he sees.

notes.258: (map): For location see Map2-B1; Map4-D3; Map5-E2; Map6-A4; Map7-C1.

rashi.heb:
*וְלֹא זֹה הָעִיר.* 
שֶׁהַנָּבִיא בְּתוֹכָהּ, וֶאֱמֶת אָמַר לָהֶם, שֶׁכְּבָר יָצָא מִמֶּנָּה.
rashi.eng: *nor is this the city.* wherein the prophet is [found]. Now he told them the truth since he had already left it.

notes.259: (tn, Heb): “and they saw, and look, [they were] in the middle of Samaria.”

notes.260: (tn, Heb): “Should I strike them down? I will strike them down.” In the Hebrew text the first person imperfect form is repeated; the first form has the interrogative he prefixed to it; the second does not. It is likely that the second form should be omitted as dittographic or that the first should be emended to an infinitive absolute.
notes.261: (tn, Heb): “my father.” The king addresses the prophet in this way to indicate his respect. See 2 Kgs 2:12.

notes.262: (tn, Heb): “Are [they] ones you captured with your sword or your bow (that) you can strike (them) down?”

rashi.heb:
*הַאֲשֶׁר שָׁבִיתָ וְגוֹ'.* 
וְכִי דַּרְכְּךָ לַהֲרֹג אוֹתָם שֶׁאַתָּה מֵבִיא שִׁבְיָה.
rashi.eng: *Do you slay those you have captured with your sword and with your bow.* Is it your custom to slay one whom you bring into captivity (and destroy them)?

rashi.heb:
*וַיִּכְרֶה.* 
לְשׁוֹן תִּקּוּן סְעוּדָה.
rashi.eng: *And he prepared.* Heb. וַיִכְרֶה an expression of preparation of a meal.

notes.266: (map): For location see Map2-B1; Map4-D3; Map5-E2; Map6-A4; Map7-C1.

notes.267: (tn, Heb): “and there was a great famine in Samaria.”
notes.268: (tn, Heb): “and look, [they] were besieging it until.”
notes.269: (tn, Heb): “eighty, silver.” The unit of measurement is omitted.
notes.270: (sn): A kab was a unit of dry measure, equivalent to approximately one quart.
notes.271: (tn): The consonantal text (Kethib) reads, “dove dung” (חֲרֵייוֹנִים, khareyonim), while the marginal reading (Qere) has “discharge” (דִּבְיוֹנִים, divyonim). Based on evidence from Akkadian, M. Cogan and H. Tadmor (II Kings [AB], 79) suggest that “dove’s dung” was a popular name for the inedible husks of seeds.
notes.272: (tn, Heb): “five, silver.” The unit of measurement is omitted.

rashi.heb:
*דִּבְיוֹנִים.* 
זֶבֶל הַזָּב מִן הַיּוֹנִים.
rashi.eng: *dove’s dung.* [Heb.] divyonim; dung that flows from the doves.

rashi.heb:
*הוֹשִׁיעָה אֲדֹנִי הַמֶּלֶךְ.* 
כְּסָבוּר שֶׁשּׁוֹאֶלֶת מְזוֹנוֹת.
rashi.eng: *“Save me, my lord the king!”.* He thought she was asking for food.

notes.273: (tn, Heb): “From where can I help you, from the threshing floor or the winepress?” The rhetorical question expresses the king’s frustration. He has no grain or wine to give to the masses.

rashi.heb:
*וַתַּחְבִּא אֶת בְּנָהּ.* 
מֵת, וְרוֹצָה לְאָכְלוֹ לְבַדָּהּ.
rashi.eng: *But she hid her son.* dead, and wants to eat him alone.

notes.274: (tn, Heb): “the people saw, and look, [there was] sackcloth against his skin underneath.”

rashi.heb:
*וַיַּרְא הָעָם.* 
דֶּרֶךְ הַקֶּרַע, אֶת הַשַּׂק תַּחַת בְּגָדָיו.
rashi.eng: *and the people saw.* the sackcloth under his garments through the tear.

notes.275: (tn, Heb): “So may God do to me, and so may he add.”
notes.276: (tn, Heb): “if the head of Elisha son of Shaphat stays on him today.”

rashi.heb:
*אִם יַעֲמֹד רֹאשׁ אֱלִישָׁע.* 
שֶׁהַיְכֹלֶת בְּיָדוֹ לְבַקֵּשׁ רַחֲמִים.
rashi.eng: *If Elisha the son of Shaphat’s head remain.* for he is able to beg for mercy.

notes.277: (tn, Heb): “and the elders were sitting with him.”
notes.278: (tn, Heb): “he”; the referent (the king) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
notes.279: (tn, Heb): “sent a man from before him, before the messenger came to him.”
notes.280: (tn, Heb): “he”; the referent (Elisha) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
notes.282: (tn, Heb): “Do you see that this son of an assassin has sent to remove my head?”
notes.283: (tn, Heb): “Is not the sound of his master’s footsteps behind him?”

rashi.heb:
*וַיִּשְׁלַח אִישׁ מִלְּפָנָיו.* 
הַמֶּלֶךְ שָׁלַח לְהָרְגוֹ, וּבְטֶרֶם יָבֹא אוֹתוֹ הַמַּלְאָךְ אֶל אֱלִישָׁע, וְהוּא נִגְלָה לוֹ בְּרוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ, וְאָמַר אֶל הַזְּקֵנִים: וְהִנֵּה הַמַּלְאָךְ יוֹרֵד אֵלָיו וְהַמֶּלֶךְ אַחֲרָיו.
rashi.eng: *and he sent a man from before him.* The king sent [a man] to kill him, and when that messenger had not yet come to Elisha, [and he was] revealed to him through the divine spirit, and he said to the elders…. and behold the messenger was coming down to him and the king was after him.

notes.284: (tn): The Hebrew text also has “look” here.
notes.286: (tn, Heb): “Look, this is a disaster from the Lord.”

rashi.heb:
*וַיֹּאמֶר.* 
הַמֶּלֶךְ.
rashi.eng: *And he said.* The king [said]

rashi.heb:
*הִנֵּה זֹאת הָרָעָה מֵאֵת ה'.* 
זֹאת אַחַת מִן הַקְּלָלוֹת שֶׁקִּלֵּל עַל יְדֵי משֶׁה: וְאָכַלְתָּ פְּרִי בִטְנְךָ בְּמָצוֹר וּבְמָצוֹק וְגוֹ'.
rashi.eng: *Behold, this calamity is from the Lord.* This is one of the curses that He cursed through Moses, (Deut. 28:53) “And you will eat the fruit of your womb… during the siege and in the straitness…”

rashi.heb:
*מָה אוֹחִיל לַה' עוֹד.* 
לְהוֹשִׁיעַ, הֲלֹא לֹא יוֹעִיל.
rashi.eng: *What more can I hope for from the Lord?.* To save? It will surely not avail.

notes.287: (sn): A seah was a dry measure equivalent to about 7 quarts.

notes.288: (tn, Heb): “the officer on whose hand the king leans.”
notes.290: (tn, Heb): “the Lord was making holes in the sky, could this thing be?” Opening holes in the sky would allow the waters stored up there to pour to the earth and assure a good crop. But, the officer argues, even if this were to happen, it would take a long time to grow and harvest the crop.
notes.291: (tn, Heb): “he”; the referent (Elisha) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
notes.292: (tn, Heb): “you will not eat from there.”

rashi.heb:
*וְאַרְבָּעָה אֲנָשִׁים.* 
גֵּיחֲזִי וּבָנָיו.
rashi.eng: *Now there were four men.* Gehazi and his sons.

rashi.heb:
*פֶּתַח הַשָּׁעַר.* 
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: בָּדָד יֵשֵׁב מִחוּץ לַמַּחֲנֵה מוֹשָׁבוֹ.
rashi.eng: *at the entrance of the gate.* as it is said (Lev. 13:46) “He shall live alone; outside the camp shall be his habitation.”

notes.295: (tn, Heb): “If we say, ‘We will enter the city,’ the famine is in the city and we will die there.”
notes.298: (tn, Heb): “we will die.” The paraphrastic translation attempts to bring out the logical force of their reasoning.

rashi.heb:
*הִשְׁמִיעַ אֶת מַחֲנֵה אֲרָם.* 
נִדְמָה לָהֶם כְּאִלּוּ שׁוֹמְעִין.
rashi.eng: *had caused the Aramean camp to hear.* It seemed to them as though they were hearing.

notes.303: (tn, Heb): “this day is a day of good news and we are keeping silent.”

rashi.heb:
*וּמְצָאָנוּ עָווֹן.* 
מִתְחַיְּבִין אָנוּ לַמַּלְכוּת.
rashi.eng: *We will incur guilt.* We will be held guilty by the throne.

notes.306: (tn): The MT has a singular form (“gatekeeper”), but the context suggests a plural. The pronoun that follows (“them”) is plural and a plural noun appears in v. 11. The Syriac Peshitta and the Targum have the plural here.
notes.307: (tn, Heb): “and, look, there was no man or voice of a man there.”
notes.308: (tn, Heb): “but the horses are tied up and the donkeys are tied up and the tents are as they were.”

rashi.heb:

Look they are like all the people of Israel” have been accidentally repeated. The original text read, “Let them take five of the remaining horses that remain in it. Look, they are like all the people of Israel that have come to an end.”

rashi.heb:
*אֲשֶׁר נִשְׁאֲרוּ בָהּ.* 
בְּתוֹךְ הָעִיר, שֶׁלֹּא מֵתוּ בָּרָעָב.

rashi.heb:
*הִנָּם כְּכָל הֲמוֹן יִשְׂרָאֵל אֲשֶׁר נִשְׁאֲרוּ בָהּ.* 
אִם יֹאמְרוּ מְסֻכָּנִין הֵם שֶׁלֹּא יַהַרְגֵם אַרָם, הֲרֵי הִנָּם בָּעִיר הַזֹּאת בְּסַכָּנַת הָרָעָב כִּשְׁאָר כָּל הֲמוֹן יִשְׂרָאֵל אֲשֶׁר נִשְׁאֲרוּ בָהּ, וְאִם יָמוּתוּ הִנָּם כְּכָל הֲמוֹן יִשְׂרָאֵל, אֲשֶׁר תָּמּוּ בָּרָעָב.
rashi.eng: *Behold, they are like all the multitude of Israel that are left there.* If they will say that they are imperiled lest the Arameans kill them, behold they are in this city in peril of famine like the rest of all the multitude of Israel that are left there, and if they die, they are like all the multitude of Israel that have perished from hunger.

*וֶאֱלִישָׁע דִּבֶּר אֶל הָאִשָּׁה.* 
זֶה שֶׁבַע שָׁנִים.

*וַיָּבֹא אֱלִישָׁע דַּמֶּשֶׂק.*

rashi.eng: *And Elisha came to Damascus.* to influence Gehazi to repent.

notes.337: (tn): The Hebrew text also has “in your hand.”
notes.338: (tn, Heb): “Inquire of the Lord through him, saying.”

notes.339: (tn, Heb): “him”; the referent (Elisha) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
notes.340: (tn): The Hebrew text also has “in his hand.”
notes.341: (tn, Heb): “and.” It is possible that the conjunction is here explanatory, equivalent to English “that is.” In this case the forty camel loads constitute the “gift” and one should translate, “He took along a gift, consisting of forty camel loads of all the fine things of Damascus.”
notes.342: (sn): The words “your son” emphasize the king’s respect for the prophet.

notes.344: (tc): The consonantal text (Kethib) reads, “Go, say, ‘Surely you will not (לֹא, lo’) recover” In this case the vav beginning the next clause should be translated, “for, because.” The marginal reading (Qere) has, “Go, say to him (לוֹ, lo), ‘You will surely recover.” In this case the vav (ו) beginning the next clause should be translated, “although, but.” The Qere has the support of some medieval Hebrew mss and the ancient versions, and is consistent with v. 14, where Hazael tells the king, “You will surely recover.” It is possible that a scribe has changed לוֹ, “to him,” to לֹא, “not,” because he felt that Elisha would not lie to the king. See M. Cogan and H. Tadmor, II Kings (AB), 90. Another possibility is that a scribe has decided to harmonize Elisha’s message with Hazael’s words in v. 14. But it is possible that Hazael, once he found out he would become the next king, decided to lie to the king to facilitate his assassination plot by making the king feel secure.

rashi.heb:
*חָיֹה תִחְיֶה.* 
כְּלַפֵּי חֲזָאֵל אָמַר, שֶׁיִּחְיֶה תַּחַת בֶּן הֲדָד לַמַּלְכוּת.
rashi.eng: *‘You will recover’.* Toward Hazael he said that he would live instead of Ben Hadad and occupy the throne.

notes.345: (tn, Heb): “he”; the referent (Elisha) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
notes.346: (tn, Heb): “and he made his face stand [i.e., be motionless] and set [his face?] until embarrassment.”

rashi.heb:
*וַיַּעֲמֵד אֶת פָּנָיו.* 
פָּנִים שֶל צַעַר שֶׁלּוֹ שֶׁהָיָה מְבַקֵּשׁ לִבְכּוֹת, הֶעֱמִיד, שֶׁלֹּא יִבְכֶּה בִּפְנֵי חֲזָאֵל, וַיָּשֶׂם לִבּוֹ לַעֲמֹד וּלְהִתְאַפֵּק.
rashi.eng: *He made his face expressionless.* [lit. he made his face stand. I.e.,] he held in his expression of grief, for he wanted to cry, so as not to cry before Hazael, and he made an effort to stand and control himself.

rashi.heb:
*עַד בּשׁ.* 
כְּמוֹ בּוֹשֵׁשׁ, וְלֹא יָכֹל לְהִתְאַפֵּק וַיֵּבְךְּ.
rashi.eng: *a long time.* ad bosh, [lit. until he delayed,] like “boshesh” (Ex. 32:1), and he could not control himself and wept.

rashi.heb:
*תְּרַטֵּשׁ.* 
לְשׁוֹן בִּקּוּעַ הַמֵּעַיִם, וְאָב לְכֻלָּן: וּקְשָׁתוֹת נְעָרִים תְּרַטַּשְׁנָה.
rashi.eng: *you will dash.* [Heb.] תְּרַטֵשׁ an expression of splitting the intestines. The origin of all of them [is] (Is. 13:18)…“and bows will split (תְּרַטֵּשְׁנָה) the youths.”

rashi.heb:
*וְהָרֹתֵיהֶם.* 
מְעֻבָּרוֹת שֶׁלָּהֶם.
rashi.eng: *and their pregnant women.* their pregnant women.

notes.347: (tn, Heb): “Indeed, what is your servant, a dog, that he could do this great thing?” With his reference to a dog, Hazael is not denying that he is a “dog” and protesting that he would never commit such a dastardly “dog-like” deed. Rather, as Elisha’s response indicates, Hazael is suggesting that he, like a dog, is too insignificant to ever be in a position to lead such conquests.

rashi.heb:
*הַמַּכְבֵּר.* 
תַּרְגּוּם יוֹנָתָן: גּוּנְכָא, וְכֵן וַתְּכַסֵּהוּ בַּשְּׂמִיכָה, תַּרְגּוּם: בְּגוּנְכָא, וְהוּא בֶּגֶד.

rashi.heb:
*וַיִּפְרֹשׂ עַל פָּנָיו.* 
לְהִצְטַנֵּן.
rashi.eng: *and spread it on his face.* so that he cool off.

notes.353: (tc): The Hebrew text reads, “and in the fifth year of Joram son of Ahab king of Israel, and [or, ‘while’?] Jehoshaphat [was?] king of Judah, Jehoram son of Jehoshaphat king of Judah became king.” The first reference to “Jehoshaphat king of Judah” is probably due to a scribe accidentally copying the phrase from the later in the verse. If the Hebrew text is retained, the verse probably refers to the beginning of a coregency between Jehoshaphat and Jehoram.

rashi.heb:
*וּבִשְׁנַת חָמֵשׁ וְגוֹ'.* 
יְהוֹשָׁפָט הִמְלִיךְ אֶת יוֹרָם בְּחַיָּיו שְׁתֵּי שָׁנִים כְּשֶׁחָזְרוּ מִן הַמִּלְחָמָה שֶׁנִּלְחֲמוּ בְּמֶלֶךְ מוֹאָב, כָּךְ שְׁנוּיָה בְּסֵדֶר עוֹלָם. בִּשְׁנַת חָמֵשׁ לִיהוֹרָם וִיהוֹשָׁפָט בִּשְׁנַת חֲמִשִּׁים, שֶׁנִּגְזְרָה גְּזֵרָה עַל יְהוֹשָׁפָט לֵהָרֵג בְּרָמוֹת גִּלְעָד, אֶלָּא שֶׁתָּלָה לוֹ בִּשְׁבִיל שֶׁזָּעַק, שֶׁבַע שָׁנִים.
rashi.eng: *And in the fifth year.* Jehoshaphat crowned Joram two years during his lifetime. When they returned from the war they had waged with the king of Moab. So it was taught in Seder Olam (ch. 17), in the fifth year of Jehoram, and as regards the fifth year since Jehoshaphat, it was decreed on Jehoshaphat to be killed in Ramoth Gilead, but he was reprieved for seven years because he cried out [to God].
